articles.title: Fifa and Netflix: Sport's next power couple?
articles.summary: The World Series began last night, with two relative minnows facing off to be crowned best team in US baseball. The Milwaukee Brewers, owned...
articles.body:
The World Series began last night, with two relative minnows facing off to be crowned best team in US baseball.

The Milwaukee Brewers, owned by credit trader turned sports team owner Mark Attanasio, are featuring in the World Series for the first time in 44 years. They are taking on the Tampa Bay Rays, owned by property developer Patrick Zalupski. The two rank 19th and 28th out of 30 teams respectively in payroll size, yet have outplayed deep-pocketed rivals that have an inherent edge in MLB's capless system. Moneyball , after all, was a baseball story.

Attanasio also owns Norwich City in English football's second tier, where the data-driven approach has not yet paid off. The Canaries sit 21st in the league table, a single point above the relegation zone. While Brighton and Brentford have successfully turned analytics into points, others are finding it far harder to reproduce the same results.

This week we explore why Fifa and Netflix could be a match made in media rights heaven. Plus, a chunky M&A deal in Spanish football. Do read on — Josh Noble, sports editor

For all the drama behind the scenes, Fifa's World Cup this summer was a commercial blockbuster. The tournament capped a four-year cycle in which football's global governing body brought in more than $15bn of revenue, while the sport itself garnered record-smashing audiences in the US.

The iron is still hot, and Fifa wants to strike. This week it launched the rights tender process in the US for the 2030 (and potentially 2034) men's World Cup.

These rights haven't been out to tender in nearly 15 years, much to the benefit of Fox. Its sports channel carried English-language coverage in the US this summer, having paid less than $500mn. The US rights for Spanish coverage fetched $600mn.

Romy Gai, chief business officer at Fifa, wouldn't be drawn on how high he thinks the rights will go for next time. On a call with journalists this week, he said they expected a big number of interested parties and that Fifa was hoping to bundle English and Spanish-language rights together.

The 2030 World Cup will be in Spain, Portugal and Morocco, making the timezone less favourable to the US audience, especially on the west coast. Fifa's own budget projects increased TV income of $800mn over the next cycle, but that is a global figure and includes other tournaments, such as the women's World Cup and the Club World Cup. Expect the increase in US rights alone to be significantly higher than that figure.

articles.summary: Man City lost to Aston Villa in Saturday's early kick-off. Champions Arsenal host Everton, before Chelsea welcomes Tottenham to Stamford Bridge.
articles.body:
Man City lost to Aston Villa in Saturday's early kick-off. Champions Arsenal host Everton, before Chelsea welcomes Tottenham to Stamford Bridge.

As always, stay right here for all the goals, highlights and other news and action from a very busy day in World Football ⬇️⬇️⬇️⬇️⬇️

Gabriel gets his first goal of the season! Just minutes earlier it looked like the Arsenal defender would succumb to injury - but no. He's now celebrating the Gunners' second after a dominant display against a toothless Everton.

Blues without star striker for London derby. Spurs mix things up with Dominic Solanke on the bench.

Ezri Konsa's early goal is enough to separate the teams at the break.

Konsa's strike is Arsenal's only effort on target from 11 attempts so far - fewer than Everton's two from three - but Mikel Arteta will be happy that his much-changed team are currently doing enough to overcome a difficult-to-beat Everton side.

Thierno Barry continues to look a nuisance, but also a player who needs multiple chances laid on for him before he'll score. David Moyes' side are lacking serious firepower in the important moments, a factor that may well decide this game.

The set piece team aren't actually THE set piece team?

That didn't take long! Konsa gets the final touch after Gabriel's header causes havoc in the Everton box. That's his first goal for the Gunners!

Man City can't quite topple Unai Emery's men.

Two goals from Nicolas Jackson compounds Enzo Maresca to an unfamiliar feeling: his first Premier League defeat as Man City manager.

While his side showed signs of fight, Aston Villa's midfield combativeness and ability to break at speed caused all kinds of issues for the club who may not even be in the division next season.

Erling Haaland's consolation header keeps him atop the goalscoring charts, but Man City have now left the door open for Arsenal to go level with them on 21 points later today when they face Everton.

Former Chelsea striker puts in stunning two-goal show to huge round of applause as he's subbed off with 10 minutes to go.

It's Jackson again! Give this man a chance and he will score right now. Just when Man City were looking set to go on and capitalise from the momentum of their goal.

Arsenal Lineup - Gyokeres Starts vs. Everton

Mikel Arteta rings the changes after a busy week defined by Bukayo Saka's injury. Riccardo Calafiori is replaced by Miles Lewis-Skelly. Viktor Gyokeres and Mikel Merino come into the starting XI.

He's barely had a touch all game. It doesn't matter. Ndiaye beats Manzambi and crosses beautifully to Haaland, who still has plenty to do. The big Norwegian rises above Lindelof and steers his header over the line.

Back underway at Villa Park. Rico Lewis and Phil Foden replace Marc Guehi and Rayan Cherki for the second 45 as Maresca looks to tighten things up.

Nicolas Jackson's goal is the difference at the break! Villa's fast start caught Man City off guard, but it's been an exciting back-and-forth since then, with chances for both teams.

Iliman Ndiaye's shot off the post is as close as the current Premier League leaders have come to scoring so far. The former Everton man also could have won a penalty, but VAR waved it away without too much stress.

Work for Enzo Maresca and his side to do in the second half.

To the tune of Outkast's 'Ms. Jackson' - I'm sorry Nic Jackson, oooh, are you for real?

What a start! Ruben Dias' poor ball leads to a miscontrol from Marc Guehi. Nicolas Jackson pounces, cuts inside Elliot Anderson and powers beyond Gianluigi Donnarumma. Super stuff!

Unai Emery's side boosted by Johan Manzambi shrugging off fitness issue. Alysson gets another start after impressive midweek performance.

articles.title: Irish Premiership: Duncan Ferguson's first game as Glentoran boss postponed
articles.summary: Duncan Ferguson's first game as Glentoran manager against Ballymena United is off because of a waterlogged pitch.
articles.body:
Duncan Ferguson's first game as Glentoran manager against Ballymena United has been postponed because of a waterlogged pitch.

The Glens were set to host the Sky Blues at the Oval on Saturday at 15:00 BST, but, after a pitch inspection at 12:00, the decision was taken to call the game off.

The Everton legend, who was confirmed as Glentoran boss on Monday , will now take charge of his new team for the first time away to Coleraine on Friday, 30 October at 19:45 GMT, live on BBC iPlayer.

A yellow Met Office weather warning is in place across Northern Ireland from 10:00 BST on Saturday until 12:00 GMT on Sunday.

There is also an amber weather warning in place for Saturday night with strong winds of up to 75mph expected.

Saturday's Women's Challenge Cup final between Glentoran and Cliftonville was also postponed on Friday because of the weather warning.

articles.title: Barnsley's all-time record appearance holder Barry 'Spud' Murphy dies
articles.summary: Barnsley have announced the death of their all-time record appearance holder Barry Murphy at the age of 86.
articles.body:
Barnsley's all-time club record appearance holder Barry Murphy has died, aged 86.

The defender played 569 games for the Tykes from 1962 to 1978 after joining them from South Shields.

Murphy continued to serve the South Yorkshire club following his retirement, as part of manager Allan Clarke's coaching staff, having become a player-coach in 1975.

He followed Clarke to Leeds United in 1980 and remained at Elland Road until 1984.

Known as "Spud", Murphy became the first substitute in Barnsley history in 1965, set a club record of 182 consecutive appearances and was named the club's player of the year in 1972.

Following his retirement, Murphy made several guest appearances at Oakwell and often hosted charity events for the club.

Barnsley's X feed said: "We are heartbroken to announce the passing of Barry Murphy, aged 86.

"An iconic full-back who was our record-appearance holder with 569 games for the Reds. Barry was a true Barnsley legend."

articles.title: Hansi Flick: "Mourinho es un gran compañero, los jugadores hablan maravillas de él"
articles.standfirst: El técnico desmenuza el estado de su vestuario en la previa del Clásico del Spotify Camp Nou
articles.summary: El técnico desmenuza el estado de su vestuario en la previa del Clásico del Spotify Camp Nou
articles.body: Hansi Flick abordó este sábado toda la actualidad culé en la previa del cruce contra el Real Madrid de mañana en el Spotify Camp Nou. El preparador alabó al equipo blanco y a Mourinho, pero se mostró seguro de que su equipo competirá a gran nivel porque ya ha superado la derrota en París en la Champions League del pasado martes. Recuperación tras París "Tengo buenas sensaciones, los jugadores se han recuperado. Están listos para el partido". Racha en LaLiga "El Clásico es distinto. Es el mejor partido que ofrece este deporte. Todo el mundo, millones de personas, tiene puesta la mirada en el encuentro. Personas de diferentes culturas, generaciones... son tres puntos pero es mucho más. Es fantástico. Mi equipo sabe cómo jugar. Estamos listos. Tengo confianza en mi equipo". Real Madrid "Espero un equipo con mucha confianza. Es un gran club. Es un bloque con grandes jugadores y con un gran entrenador. Así lo veo. Tiene futbolistas fantásticos, sobre todo en el último tercio. Tenemos que estar listos". Arbitraje "No creo que los comentarios afecten a los árbitros. Confío plenamente en ellos. El arbitraje es de calidad. Es muy importante proteger a los nuestros, y también a ellos. No quiero hablar más de esto". Derrota en París "Hemos hablado con los jugadores, hemos analizado el encuentro. Hicimos cosas muy bien, pero hay situaciones que debemos mejorar. Tenemos que crecer. Mañana jugamos contra uno de los mejores equipos del mundo, es una oportunidad para crecer como equipo". Mourinho "Le tengo el mayor respeto. Cuando uno gestiona equipos a este nivel y demuestra estos éxitos... estamos hablando de calidad. Le visité cuando estuve en la selección, y todos los jugadores hablan maravillas de él. Es un gran compañero, con éxito". Koundé y Olmo "Jules no estará mañana. No queremos arriesgar. Es una situación que hay que aceptar. Y Dani estaba en un gran momento, en forma. No ha tenido suerte. Pero hay que aceptarlo también, él no está contento. Se perderá muchos partidos. Tenemos a Fermín. Nos aportan los dos gran calidad". Goles de estrategia "Sabemos los puntos fuertes del Real Madrid, y en las jugadas de estrategia es uno de los mejores equipos. También son fuertes físicamente. Hay que defender mejor que en París. Lo hemos comentado hoy". Rodri "Siempre nos centramos en nuestro equipo, y al ver que podíamos ficharlo sabíamos que nos ayudaría. Es una pieza que nos aporta mucho. Lo hemos visto ya en los primeros partidos. Vemos su impacto en el equipo y en el club, y estoy contento de que esté aquí. Él y Pedri nos aportan calidad en la medular". Xavier Espart "Todos sabemos que es un profesional. Lo ha hecho muy bien en ambos lados de la defensa. Para mí es un jugador increíble, pero tiene margen de mejora. Tiene potencial. Su rendimiento es bueno, pero debe seguir demostrándolo". Mbappé "Lo importante es posicionarnos bien con y sin balón. Y tener una buena distancia entre futbolistas, presionar con el jugador con balón... si lo hacemos todo bien será fácil defender las jugadas del Real Madrid. Cubarsí y Gerard están jugando muy bien. Lo que hacen es increíble. Están creciendo juntos. Estoy muy contento". Discurso Real Madrid "Prefiero centrarme en preparar a mi equipo, no me preocupan estas cosas. No me preocupan los titulares".

articles.title: Barcelona vs Real Madrid: Top 5 El Clasico matches between La Liga giants
articles.summary: Matches between Barca and Real are among the biggest in world football, with their rivalry spanning more than a century.
articles.body:
One of football’s oldest rivalries will be in the spotlight this weekend, as Barcelona host Real Madrid in Sunday’s blockbuster showdown.

Famously dubbed El Clasico – Spanish for “The Classic” – fixtures between the La Liga giants have historically drawn millions of viewers worldwide, with many of the world’s best players featuring.

From duels between Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo, two of football’s finest players, to Neymar Jr, Luis Suarez, David Beckham and Zinedine Zidane, fans have been spoiled for choice.

In recent years, the limelight has shifted to Lamine Yamal and Raphinha of Barcelona and Kylian Mbappe, Jude Bellingham and Vinicius Jr in the Real camp.

With a rivalry dating back to 1902, Barcelona and Real are familiar foes and victory on the pitch often brings bragging rights that extend far beyond football.

The clubs have 106 wins each, setting the perfect stage for the upcoming El Clasico, where three points will give one of them the edge in their storied rivalry.

Ahead of the latest Barcelona vs Real, Al Jazeera looks back at their top five clashes:

Real Madrid 2-3 Barcelona (April 23, 2017 – La Liga)

Our list begins with an all-time classic.

This match ranks among Barcelona fans’ fondest victories, with a stoppage-time Messi strike giving them an El Clasico win over Real.

Real took the lead at the Santiago Bernabeu stadium when Casemiro scored in the first half, but Messi equalised within five minutes.

Ivan Rakitic then scored after the break as Barca came from behind to take the lead and things went from bad to worse for the hosts after captain Sergio Ramos was sent off for a two-footed lunge on Messi.

Real fans breathed a sigh of relief when James Rodriguez netted in the 85th minute, but Messi silenced the crowd, scoring the winner with the last kick of the game to bring up his 500th Barca goal.

The thriller went down as one of the best Clasicos in history, with end-to-end action from the off.

While victory momentarily put Barca on top of the table, Real went on to be crowned champions of Spain that season, finishing three points above their Catalan rivals.

Barcelona 3-3 Real Madrid (March 10, 2007 – La Liga)

This Camp Nou fixture offered fans the first glimpse of Messi’s wizardry on the field.

A 19-year-old Messi, still far from a finished product, scored his first career hat-trick against Real that day, salvaging a draw for the hosts, who ended the game with 10 men.

Real’s Ruud van Nistelrooy scored twice in the first half and Ramos added another in the second, but Messi ensured that Barca earned a draw, scoring the equaliser in the first minute of stoppage time.

The Argentinian’s coming-of-age performance foreshadowed the dominance that would follow.

Interestingly, Real and Barca ended the season on equal points (76), but Real won the title thanks to a superior head-to-head record against Barca.

Real Madrid 4-2 Barcelona (April 10, 2005 – La Liga)

The next game on our list saw Real win in style.

Los Blancos sealed an emphatic victory at home with their Galacticos, the mega-expensive world-class talent bought by President Florentino Perez, adding glamour to the fixture.

French great Zinedine Zidane scored early and Brazil’s Ronaldo Nazario doubled the advantage, before Raul netted another. Michael Owen then sealed the deal with his 65th-minute winner.

Several of Real’s superstars, such as Beckham, Roberto Carlos, Luis Figo and Iker Casillas, also graced the field that day.

While Samuel Eto’o and Ronaldinho were on the scoresheet for Barca, it wasn’t enough as Real stormed to victory. However, it was Barcelona who went on to win the league title that season, finishing three points clear at the top.

Real Madrid 2-6 Barcelona (May 2, 2009 – La Liga)

The dynamic duo of Thierry Henry and Messi ran riot for Barca in this game, breaking the hearts of the Real faithful at the Bernabeu.

When Gonzalo Higuain put Real in the lead in the 14th minute, Real fans were optimistic about a good result. But it didn’t take too long to turn into pessimism as Henry equalised within four minutes.

What came next was nothing short of a goal-fest as Henry completed his brace, Messi followed suit, while Carles Puyol and Gerard Pique also joined the party with a goal apiece.

Ramos’ second-half goal carried very little meaning in the game, as Real were crushed by their rivals on their own turf.

Barca would go on to comfortably win the league that season, finishing nine points ahead of Real.

Real Madrid 1-0 Barcelona (April 20, 2011 – Copa del Rey final)

Our list wraps up with a Ronaldo special and one that clinched a trophy for Real.

The 2011 Copa del Rey final featured a sensational El Clasico that ended in dramatic fashion.

With the game still goalless after 90 minutes, the match went to extra time and many thought a penalty shootout would decide the final’s fate.

But then came Ronaldo’s moment of magic. The Portugal international headed home superbly from an Angel Di Maria pass, securing Real’s first trophy under then-manager Jose Mourinho.

Even though Di Maria was soon sent off after picking up his second yellow card, it did little harm as Ronaldo’s header brought home Real’s first domestic cup since 1993.

articles.body: el Betis vuelve a poner el 'modo Liga' tras una nueva victoria en la Champions League, en este caso ante el Feyenoord en La Cartuja, y lo hace con la visita al Celta de Vigo. Manuel Pellegrini ha comparecido este mediodía en rueda de prensa para valorar el encuentro, el estado del plantel y otro temas y nombres propios de la actualidad verdiblanca. El técnico chileno confirmó las bajas de Junior y Cucho. "Junior está avanzando y la semana que viene se integrará con el plantel y a Cucho difícil que vuelva antes del parón. Hay que ver su evolución, es un tema muscular y diría que para esa fecha estaría", valoró el chileno. Dani Ceballos. "Se ha ido incorporado a un funcionamiento futbolístico. Llevaba un tiempo largo sin entrenar y jugar. Va por el camino correcto y ha ido mejorando sus prestaciones. Ya veremos cómo evoluciona en cuanto a minutos". Lo Celso. "Jugó un rato contra el Barcelona. En ese rato hizo un gol, que fue anulado, dejó mano a mano a Abdé con el portero en el gol que convertimos y dejó otro mano a mano a Cucho que atajó el portero. Más no se le puede pedir a jugadores con esa calidad. Después, por supuesto, también hay un trabajo en equipo que se ha ido a poco adaptando. Va mejorando día tras día, igual que Dani Ceballos van teniendo minutos. Son muchos los partidos, así que entre todos tenemos que sacar esto adelante". Antony y su falta de calma en los metros finales. "Creo que Antony autoexigencia tiene en este momento y le sobra. Es un jugador que está corriendo mucho, que está recuperando balones, que está metido en muchas jugadas. A lo mejor por un exceso de ansiedad le está faltando ese pase final o esa definición final, pero es un jugador que en el funcionamiento del equipo nos está aportando mucho y ya se le saldrán los goles y los pases finales que te lo hace con tanta precisión, así que él está muy consciente y está tratando de corregirlo y mejorarlo". Alternativa a Marc Roca. "Lo de Marc, justamente, lo hemos ido adaptando a esa posición. Sin Facundo habrá que buscar otra alternativa porque son muchos partidos para que lo juegue todo Marc, pero veremos cómo se va recuperando y quién podría reemplazarlo. Es un tema que se habló con anterioridad. Es cierto que es un puesto que ha tenido cierto déficit anteriormente. Pudimos formar a Marc Roca y ya veremos si algún otro se puede adaptar a esa situación, seguramente sí. Lo veremos en los entrenamientos". El rival, el Celta. "Viene con la moral muy arriba, en un recinto complicado. El Celtic se hace respetar en casa. Horas más o menos, desgasta jugar el jueves y luego domingo, pero no es algo decisivo para la competición. No podemos esperar encontrar un rival más fácil porque llegó más tarde". Nivel de la plantilla. "Estoy muy contento con la plantilla que tenemos en estos momentos, igual que en años anteriores. Es injusto comparar un momento con una temporada. No sé si era mejor o no pero consiguió la Champions, igual que hace años atrás se ganó la copa. No hay que comprar, los momentos son distintos. Estamos en un momento en el que la plantilla está pasando un buen momento y eso me permite tener más variantes. No hay un once titular, porque todos cuando salen están con un rendimiento alto y es lo que uno exige todos los días en los entrenamientos. Tenemos que mantener esos rendimientos individuales en las tres competiciones. Para mí es más fácil hacer rotaciones mientras estén todos involucrados". Posición de Lo Celso contra el Barcelona. "Yo creo que los medios de calidad, cuando van en una banda, hacen mucho daño a los equipos contrarios. Lo hemos hecho con Lo Celso, Canales y también con equipos anteriores, con el mismo Isco o Cazorla, con teóricos ‘10’ cargados a banda y con libertad de movimientos. Gio lo hizo muy bien, como lo puede hacer Dani Ceballos o Álvaro Fidalgo. Son variantes dentro del plantel". Isco. "El nivel de Isco es indudable, pero tenía que superar los dolores. Por suerte ahora ya no hay dolor y seguimos viendo su calidad de forma más continuada y con muchos más minutos".

articles.standfirst: Tras 37 días sin Liga en el Sánchez-Pizjuán, el Sevilla recibe a Osasuna en su feudo, donde los rojillos solo han ganado una vez en veinte años
articles.summary: Tras 37 días sin Liga en el Sánchez-Pizjuán, el Sevilla recibe a Osasuna en su feudo, donde los rojillos solo han ganado una vez en veinte años
articles.body: El Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán volverá a vestirse de gala el próximo lunes para el retorno de la competición liguera. Tras un periplo marcado por las salidas al Ciutat de València y al Santiago Bernabéu justo después del parón internacional, el Sevilla buscará reencontrarse con el triunfo delante de su afición. Enfrente tendrá a Osasuna, que afronta su segundo partido desde el regreso al banquillo de Jagoba Arrasate, pero que históricamente ha encontrado en el feudo hispalense un territorio especialmente hostil. El balance de las visitas de Osasuna al Sevilla habla por sí solo, ya sea en el Estadio de Nervión, en el Sánchez-Pizjuán o incluso en Chapín (2002-03). En 57 encuentros oficiales, los andaluces han cosechado 36 victorias, 14 empates y siete derrotas. A pesar de que los navarros arañaron puntos en tres temporadas consecutivas (2022-2025), la tendencia reciente es contundente a favor de los locales, que han cedido tres empates y una derrota en los últimos veinte años; aquel triunfo rojillo se produjo precisamente bajo la dirección de Arrasate. La pasada campaña, el Sevilla pudo romper su mala racha frente a Osasuna gracias a un penalti cometido sobre Juanlu Sánchez y transformado por Rubén Vargas (1-0). De hecho, el internacional suizo, con muchas posibilidades de mantener la titularidad en la banda derecha, no marca como sevillista desde aquel partido. El partido de este lunes pondrá fin a 37 días sin Liga en el Sánchez-Pizjuán, pues la última cita oficial del Sevilla en su casa fue el 19 de septiembre ante el Barcelona. Desde entonces, la hinchada únicamente ha podido acudir a su templo para el Trofeo Antonio Puerta frente al Aston Villa de Unai Emery. La vuelta a Nervión marca el pistoletazo de salida para una fase del calendario crucial, en la que el conjunto dirigido por Luis García Plaza necesita hacerse fuerte de nuevo en su estadio.

articles.body: El Valencia afronta el derbi autonómico con la necesidad de sumar los tres puntos para salir de los puestos de descenso. El conjunto dirigido por Javier Aguirre no ha tenido un buen arranque liguero y se encuentra en la penúltima posición con seis puntos. Por su parte, el Villarreal llega al encuentro con la intención de sumar tres puntos que le permitan escalar posiciones en la tabla. El conjunto valencianista no ha logrado ganar ninguno de sus últimos cinco enfrentamientos ligueros ante el cuadro amarillo, con un balance de dos empates y tres derrotas, y nunca ha encadenado seis partidos sin vencerle en la máxima categoría. Además, cayó por 0-2 en el último duelo disputado en Mestalla, en octubre de 2025, poniendo fin a una racha de siete encuentros seguidos como local sin perder frente al Villarreal (cinco victorias y dos empates). Pese a ello, el Valencia ha mostrado una mejoría en las últimas jornadas y ha puntuado en tres de sus cuatro compromisos más recientes en LaLiga, tras enlazar previamente cuatro derrotas consecutivas. Después del 2-2 ante el Racing de Santander y el 0-0 frente al Athletic, el equipo de Javier Aguirre tiene la posibilidad de encadenar tres empates seguidos en la competición por primera vez desde noviembre de 2021. El Villarreal, por su parte, atraviesa un inicio de curso irregular, con nueve puntos en las nueve primeras jornadas, y llega tras dos encuentros consecutivos sin marcar, una situación que podría prolongarse por tercera fecha seguida por primera vez desde diciembre de 2016. El partido entre Valencia y Villarreal se juega el sábado 24 de octubre a las 18:30 horas. El partido entre Valencia y Villarreal de la jornada 10 de LaLiga EA Sports se podrá ver por televisión en directo a través de Movistar LaLiga. También se podrá seguir el partido a través de la narración de Radio MARCA y con los comentarios en directo de MARCA.com. Desde dos horas antes, sigue la previa y los onces. Tras el encuentro, podrás leer la crónica, las declaraciones de los protagonistas y ver el resumen con las mejores jugadas y los goles. El Valencia llega al partido de LaLiga EA Sports contra el Villarreal tras empatar contra el Athletic Club, se encuentra en la posición 19 de LaLiga EA Sports con 6 puntos. El Villarreal llega al partido de LaLiga EA Sports contra el Valencia tras empatar contra el Elche, se encuentra en la posición 12 de LaLiga EA Sports con 9 puntos.

articles.body: El Clásico del domingo en el Camp Nou invita a Mourinho a afinar cada pieza, y su once probable deja entrever un plan muy definido. Con Courtois como guardián, el portugués mantendría a Valverde en el lateral derecho, el puesto que el capitán ha hecho suyo en los dos últimos encuentros pese a no ser su hábitat natural, en una zaga que completarían Konaté, Huijsen y Cucurella. Por delante, un doble pivote con Tchouaméni y Camavinga sostendría a una línea de tres—Güler, Bellingham y Diomande— al servicio de Mbappé. La ausencia de Vinicius, sancionado, obliga a reordenar el ataque: Diomande, que llega lanzado tras su golazo al Leipzig, heredaría la banda izquierda. Por otro lado, Güler se abriría a la derecha, aunque el turco suele moverse también por zonas interiores para tejer el juego.. La gran incógnita, y a la vez la apuesta más significativa, apunta a Eduardo Camavinga. El francés apenas ha gozado de protagonismo en este arranque de curso, pero sus características encajan como un guante en el plan que Mourinho dibuja para una cita de tanto voltaje. En Valdebebas valoran su poderío físico, su conducción y esa facilidad para romper líneas con el balón cosido al pie como armas idóneas tanto para contener la presión del Barça como para lanzar al Madrid en las transiciones, la vía por la que los blancos confían en hacer más daño en territorio hostil.

articles.standfirst: La máxima rivalidad del fútbol español mantiene un pulso histórico marcado por la máxima igualdad en todos sus enfrentamientos
articles.summary: La máxima rivalidad del fútbol español mantiene un pulso histórico marcado por la máxima igualdad en todos sus enfrentamientos
articles.body: El enfrentamiento entre el Barcelona y el Real Madrid representa uno de los acontecimientos con mayor seguimiento en el planeta deportivo. Cada temporada, la retransmisión de este histórico choque llega a más de ciento noventa países, paralizando el mundo durante noventa minutos para seguir la actuación de las grandes estrellas. Los orígenes ligueros de esta rivalidad se remontan a febrero de 1929 en el campo de Les Corts. En aquella primera edición del torneo, el conjunto merengue logró la victoria por un gol a dos, aunque el cuadro catalán devolvió el triunfo en la segunda vuelta del campeonato. En el cómputo global de todas las competiciones oficiales, la igualdad entre ambas entidades es máxima a lo largo del tiempo. Tras disputarse un total de doscientos sesenta y tres partidos, el balance arroja exactamente ciento cinco victorias para el Barcelona por ciento seisr del Real Madrid. Centrando el análisis únicamente en el torneo de LaLiga, el Real Madrid domina con ochenta victorias frente a las setenta y siete logradas por el Barcelona. En el apartado goleador de la competición regular, el conjunto culé lidera ligeramente la estadística por trescientos doce goles anotados frente a trescientos nueve.

articles.title: Borja Jiménez toma el mando del Cádiz: “Sé dónde vengo, miedo ninguno”
articles.standfirst: El nuevo técnico prioriza salir del descenso y ganar al Ceuta, pero avisa que necesita semanas para que el equipo haga "más cosas de las que nosotros queremos"
articles.summary: El nuevo técnico prioriza salir del descenso y ganar al Ceuta, pero avisa que necesita semanas para que el equipo haga "más cosas de las que nosotros queremos"
articles.body: El Cádiz ha vivido una semana acelerada desde la derrota en Granada. El lunes destituyó a Albert Celades, que dejó al equipo en descenso con siete puntos de 30, y Mario Fuentes asumió los entrenamientos mientras se cerraba la llegada de Borja Jiménez. El abulense participó a distancia desde Qatar, donde el jueves dirigió su último partido con el Al-Ahli, un empate ante el Al-Gharafa. Después llegó el anuncio oficial, una noche de viaje y su primera sesión presencial el viernes en El Rosal. Y este sábado ha sido presentado en la Tacita de Plata, con el Ceuta esperando a poco más de 24 horas el domingo como examen. Borja Jiménez aterriza con las prioridades ordenadas. “El primer objetivo es muy claro, que es salir de donde estamos. El equipo necesita ganar”, afirmó, y no quiso abrir debates sobre metas más lejanas: “El primer mensaje que hemos mandado desde el minuto uno es Ceuta. Intentar ponernos un objetivo ahora no tendría sentido cuando no hemos tenido tiempo para trabajar”. El técnico tampoco promete una transformación inmediata. “No vamos a ver un cambio radical porque llevamos muy poquito tiempo, pero sí vamos a intentar que haya matices”. Distingue entre las primeras señales y la construcción de su propuesta: “Veremos un equipo reconocible en seis, siete semanas”, aunque asegura que “mañana ya veremos un Cádiz reconocible”. Recibe una plantilla “muy variada, con diferentes perfiles en todas las líneas” y acepta la presión de un banquillo por el que han pasado cinco entrenadores este año. “Sé dónde vengo, miedo ninguno. La paciencia con los entrenadores es muy limitada y eso lo asumimos con total normalidad”. También pidió el respaldo de la grada. “Entiendo el enfado que puedan tener, pero es importante que nos ayuden porque lo vamos a necesitar”. Sobre la portería, dejó una certeza y ninguna pista: “Tengo claro cuál es el portero. No te lo voy a decir”. Por su lado, Javier Muiños, director de fútbol del conjunto amarillo, explicó que el Cádiz se decidió por Borja desde que conoció su disposición a salir de Qatar. “Se adapta perfectamente a lo que tenemos. Es un entrenador capaz de que el jugador interprete lo que necesita el partido”, defendió. La espera, reconoció, “se nos ha hecho un poquito larga”, pero la elección nunca ofreció dudas: “Teníamos muy claro que queríamos que fuese él”.

articles.title: Aston Villa 2-1 Man City: How the players rated
articles.summary: How Aston Villa and Man City players rated following their Premier League match.
articles.body:
Nicolas Jackson scored twice as Aston Villa ended Manchester City's 100% winning start to the Premier League season.

Here's how I rated the players and how you rated the players.

What do BBC Sport's player ratings mean?

Zion Suzuki: Good in the air, decent distribution and made three important stops to deny Iliman Ndiaye, Rayan Cherki and Josko Gvardiol with a brilliant, fingertip save. 7

Matty Cash: Battled all game with Jeremy Doku and though he was booked for a push on the Belgian, he managed more tackles than any other player. 7

Victor Lindelof: Threw his body at everything that came his way but outmuscled for Haaland's goal. 6

Pau Torres: Calming presence at the back without being too ruffled. 6

Ian Maatsen: Could have scored early on but blazed a volley over. Vital header away to deny Erling Haaland's goalbound header late on. 6

John McGinn: Picked off Marc Guehi to lay on the opening goal and created more chances than anyone else on the pitch. 7

Boubacar Kamara: At the heart of everything good from the home side, sniffing out the danger. 7

Joao Gomes: Mucked in alongside Kamara by keeping the ball ticking and contributing three interceptions. 6

Alysson: The 20-year-old Brazilian impressed against Viking in the Champions League and showed why he was given a start again with another eye-catching performance. 7

Johan Manzambi: Switzerland international displayed sparks of his undoubted talent and could have had a penalty in the first half. 6

Nicolas Jackson: Brimming with confidence. Took the opening goal brilliantly, firing high into the roof of the net, before stroking in a second. 9

Ibrahim Mbaye (on 58, Alysson) Instant impact after coming on, providing a low cross for Jackson to finish. 7

Subs not used: Marco Bizot, Tyrone Mings, Lamare Bogarde, George Hemmings.

Gianluigi Donnarumma: Conceded an early corner after taking too long over a goal-kick, poor kicking often put team-mates in trouble and should have done better for the second goal. 5

Abdukodir Khusanov: Shaky at right-back before being moved into central defence for the second half. 6

Ruben Dias: Rattled by Jackson in the first half but made a good block to deny Alysson a certain goal. 5

Marc Guehi: Another shocker. Culpable for both of Ipswich's goals last weekend and made another poor error which led to Villa's opener. Booked for hauling down Jackson on the edge of the box before being taken off at half-time. 4

Josko Gvardiol: Given a difficult time by Alysson throughout but came close to scoring in the second half. 5

Elliot Anderson: Struggled to impose himself in the game and was shown a yellow card for a mis-timed challenge on Gomes. 6

Enzo Fernandez: Always available for the ball but lost the midfield battle. 6

Iliman Ndiaye: City's liveliest player. Showed quick footwork to force Suzuki into a decent save, clipped the post with another similar effort and provided the cross for Haaland's equaliser. 8

Jeremy Doku: Looked to create openings with his box of tricks but often wasteful. 6

Rayan Cherki: Often crowded out by Villa's midfield and booked for a frustrated tug on Manzambi. Subbed at half-time. 5

Erling Haaland: Quiet in the first half but came to life in the second with a towering header to draw his side level. 7

Phil Foden (on 46, Cherki) Had little impact after Tuesday's Champions League hat-trick. 6

Rico Lewis (on 46, Guehi) Pushed forward but unable to make a meaningful contribution. 6

Subs not used: Geronimo Rulli, Mateo Kovacic, Rayan Ait-Nouri, Vitor Reis, Ayyoub Bouaddi, Nico O'Reilly.

After the opportunity to rate players has closed, the score displayed represents the average from all the submissions by BBC Sport users.

articles.title: Nico Jackson y Suzuki prolongan la 'maldición' de Villa Park y rompen el invicto del Manchester City
articles.standfirst: Los de Unai Emery provocan la primera derrota de los 'cityzens' en Premier, que ya acumulan su quinta temporada sin ganar en Birmingham
articles.summary: Los de Unai Emery provocan la primera derrota de los 'cityzens' en Premier, que ya acumulan su quinta temporada sin ganar en Birmingham
articles.body: El Manchester City llegaba a Villa Park con su pleno de victorias histórico en las siete primeras jornadas. Los de Maresca visitaban el estadio 'maldito' que tanto le ha costado conquistar a los 'cityzen' en los últimos años; desde 2021 no saben lo que es ganar en el campo del Aston Villa, coincidiendo casi en su totalidad desde la incorporación de Unai Emery al conjunto de Birmingham. Y no iba a ser otro que el técnico de Hondarribia el que amargara el perfecto inicio de temporada 'sky blue'. Los locales arrancaron con una presión intensa desde el inicio, y no tardaron en recoger los frutos. Un error en la salida de balón de Guéhi propició el primer gol del partido. McGinn robó, y Nico Jackson liquidó. El delantero senegalés realizó una gran maniobra para fusilar a Donnaruma y poner en ventaja a los suyos en el minuto seis. El Manchester City tuvo que reaccionar y empezó a poner en aprietos al Aston Villa, sofocado sin poder salir de su área pero sostenido por un solvente Suzuki. A la buena actuación del meta nipón se le sumó la fortuna del palo. Un disparo de Iliman Ndiaye desde la banda derecha, que recortó hacia dentro para disparar con la zurda, se estrelló contra la madera a la media hora. El equipo de Unai Emery consiguió resistir las acometidas de un City que no conseguía encontrar a Haaland, bastante desaparecido. Pero un 'killer' como el noruego no es que necesite mucho para ser decisivo en un partido. A los siete minutos de la reanudación, Haaland voló para bajar de las nubes con un cabezazo el centro de Ndiaye desde la derecha y batir por primera vez a Suzuki, que tuvo que seguir empleándose a fondo ante los dos disparos a bocajarro de Gvardiol. Y de senegaleses iba la cosa. Emery introdujo en el minuto 60 a Ibrahim Mbaye, que apenas tardó un minuto en atacar la banda derecha y servir en bandeja el gol a su compatriota Jackson, que hizo su doblete particular. El Aston Villa, que ya parece haber encontrado de nuevo velocidad de crucero, se limitó a sacar piernas frescas y hacerse fuerte en su área para proteger el resultado. El Manchester City pierde sus primeros puntos de la temporada y deja en siete las victorias consecutivas a manos de un Aston Villa que ya acumula más de un mes sin conocer la derrota entre todas las competiciones. La 'maldición' de Villa Park para los 'cityzens' seguirá, como mínimo, una temporada más.

articles.title: 'Save Women’s Sports' activists ejected from NWSL match after being struck, confronted by pro-trans crowd
articles.summary: XX-XY Athletics supporters say they were physically struck before getting escorted out of a Portland Thorns NWSL game after unveiling a "Save Women's Sports" banner.
articles.body: Around 20 "Save Women's Sports" activists wearing XX-XY Athletics shirts were forcibly escorted out of a Portland Thorns match on Friday night after members of the group were struck and verbally berated by other fans during a demonstration supporting female-only sports. The confrontation occurred during the Thorns’ match against the North Carolina Courage at Providence Park in Portland, Oregon. The club’s schedule designated the match as its "Fan Appreciation" night. According to a preliminary account, the group entered with their XX-XY shirts covered and kept them concealed through the first half. At the start of the second half, they revealed the shirts and unfurled a large banner reading "Save Women’s Sports," but matters quickly escalated from that point on. FANS DISAGREE WITH PORTLAND THORNS OVER REASON FOR EJECTION IN XX-XY APPAREL DISPUTE: 'THEY ARE LYING' Other spectators, described in the account as supporters of transgender inclusion in women’s sports, allegedly responded with verbal abuse and physical aggression, including striking members of the group with flagpoles carrying trans flags. Security subsequently escorted the roughly 20 demonstrators out of the stadium. The organizers included women’s sports activist Amy Sousa and commentator Brandi Kruse, who previously helped organize rallies supporting WNBA player Sophie Cunningham. Sousa told OutKick that she and other XX-XY Athletics attendees filed police reports after being escorted out of the stadium. "We were attacked by fans. We were hit with flags. We had drinks and thrown at us," said Sousa, standing behind police outside the stadium because she did not feel safe. "Other people were forcibly pushed out the door. We had an ADA woman in a walker, she was forcibly pushed out the door. They let these people hit us with flags, another woman was punched in the face, all because we wanted to stand there in our shirts to protect girls sports." This wasn't the first time Sousa and XX-XY Athletics supporters had been ejected from a Thorns game at Providence Park. A smaller group was removed in early September, when Sousa said she was accused of being "transphobic" for her pro-women apparel. WNBA FANS RECALL EJECTION THREAT OVER XX-XY ATHLETICS SHIRT AT FEVER-DREAM GAME: 'I WAS FLABBERGASTED' The decision to unfurl the "Save Women's Sports" banner and reveal their shirts at the start of the second half Friday was strategic. Sousa hoped the group could avoid ejection because soccer has no official breaks in play. But members of the Rose City Riveters — the Thorns' emphatically pro-trans supporters group — appeared to have caught wind of their intentions. Just before the second half began, a number of fans were given transgender pride flags, apparently in an effort to obstruct other spectators' view of the banner and XX-XY supporters. One man sitting across the aisle from the group repeatedly shouted, "F--- you! F--- you, scum!" Chants of "Trans lives matter!" followed. OutKick reporter Matt Calkins, who was credentialed for the match, attempted to document the confrontation but was also subjected to verbal and physical aggression. He was flipped off, called a Nazi, had his phone knocked out of his hand and had beer poured on his neck. The interaction was captured by Calkins on video. XX-XY attendees weren't treated much better. Kruse had her right arm restrained behind her back by a security guard, who walked her up the stairs to the concourse and out of the stadium. This happened after she said she and others were hit multiple times with flags, with the assaulters repeatedly acting like it was an accident. Kruse added that another XX-XY attendee was pushed over her seat and "tumbled down." Aside from one man who poured beer on someone, Brandi said no other assaulters were removed. "I asked the security guard 'Why are we being asked to leave and they're not not being asked to leave?' If you want all of us to leave that's another thing, but just us? So I said 'I'm not leaving on my own accord'," Kruse said. "So two security guards grabbed me and took me out. I'm in shock over it." TRANS ACTIVISTS HARASS, HURL SLURS AT SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SUPPORTERS BEFORE FEVER GAME IN MINNESOTA A separate security guard also yanked an Calkins' credential from around his neck as he interviewed Sousa. The guard returned it seconds later but declined to explain his actions when questioned. Director of security Jim McCausland was texted for comment, per OutKick's request, but said he did not have time to talk. OutKick also reached to the Thorns' communication director for comment — specifically as to why XX-XY attendees were escorted out but not their assaulters — but received no response. Roughly half a dozen XX-XY supporters left the stadium before the banner was even revealed, fearing for their safety after seeing spectators wearing "Protect Trans Kids" shirts featuring images of knives. But Ari Laureano, who has detransitioned, chose to stay. Laureano said just after he unbuttoned his coat to reveal his XX-XY shirt, he was smashed in the face by a flagpole. He added that assaulters used flags as a barricade to hide that they were striking the women he was with. Worth it to try and make a change? In Laureano's mind, yes. But he doesn't expect much sympathy from journalists. "I think the average person looks at this and doesn't understand what's going on, and the media goes and calls all these women horrible homophobic bigots," Laureano said. "But I'm here with them as a gay man who was harmed by being transitioned young, and I'm being beaten alongside of them. These are just normal impacted women who care about women's sports." ZERO BS. Additionally, Washington and Colorado have measures on their Nov. 3 ballots that would restrict participation in school sports based on biological sex. Washington's initiative applies to K-12 athletics, while Colorado's would extend to college sports. articles.title: Samu Castillejo anuncia su retirada
articles.standfirst: El atacante malagueño lo deja con 31 años
articles.summary: El atacante malagueño lo deja con 31 años
articles.body: Samu Castillejo pone punto final a su carrera profesional a los 31 años. El futbolista malagueño ha anunciado su retirada a través de un emotivo vídeo publicado en sus redes sociales, después de permanecer sin equipo desde la pasada temporada, cuando terminó su etapa en el Johor FC de Malasia. El extremo se formó en la cantera del Málaga CF, donde comenzó a llamar la atención con el Atlético Malagueño antes de dar el salto al primer equipo con apenas 19 años. Fue durante la temporada 2014/2015 cuando se consolidó en el fútbol profesional, disputando 39 encuentros y firmando un gol y cinco asistencias. Su rendimiento despertó el interés del Villarreal, que terminó pagando alrededor de ocho millones de euros por su incorporación. A partir de ahí comenzó una trayectoria lejos de La Rosaleda que le llevó por algunos de los grandes escenarios del fútbol europeo. AC Milan, Valencia CF y Sassuolo fueron sus siguientes destinos antes de emprender la aventura asiática con el Johor FC, donde cerró su última etapa como futbolista. Su posible regreso a Málaga llegó a estar sobre la mesa en el verano de 2024. Castillejo fue ofrecido en varias ocasiones para volver a vestir de blanquiazul, aunque finalmente Loren Juarros descartó la operación. El malagueño se marcha después de 412 partidos, 49 goles y 30 asistencias en el fútbol profesional. Internacional con las categorías inferiores de la selección española, Castillejo pone así el broche a una carrera que comenzó en Martiricos y que le llevó posteriormente a competir en España, Italia y Malasia.

articles.title: Edin Terzic: “Mi trabajo no es buscar excusas, es encontrar soluciones”
articles.standfirst: El club afronta una nueva oportunidad para reencontrarse con la victoria después de cuatro partidos consecutivos sin ganar.
articles.summary: El club afronta una nueva oportunidad para reencontrarse con la victoria después de cuatro partidos consecutivos sin ganar.
articles.body: El Athletic afronta una nueva oportunidad para reencontrarse con la victoria después de cuatro partidos consecutivos sin ganar. Los rojiblancos reciben al Getafe en San Mamés con la necesidad de mejorar sus últimas actuaciones y recuperar sensaciones tras la derrota ante el Levante. En la previa del encuentro, Edin Terzic ha repasado la situación del equipo, las bajas, los problemas ofensivos y la presión que rodea al conjunto bilbaíno. Estado de la plantilla: “Aymeric (Laporte) está sancionado y no estará disponible. Sabemos que Guruzeta se va a perder buena parte de la temporada, quizá toda. Sancet tampoco estará mañana, pero está en la última fase de su recuperación”. Sancet: “Esperamos que el lunes o el martes empiece a entrenar más con el grupo y esté preparado para la próxima semana”. El partido ante el Getafe como una final: “No tengo ningún problema en llamar finales a los partidos. Si juegas cada encuentro como si fuera el último de la temporada, no hay ningún problema. Entiendo perfectamente lo que ha dicho Iñaki. Cuando estás en un club grande y llevas tres partidos sin ganar y pierdes el cuarto, la presión aumenta. Somos plenamente conscientes de ello. Pero lo más importante no es lo que digamos antes del partido, sino lo que demostremos mañana sobre el césped”. Preocupación por los resultados: “Mi trabajo no es buscar excusas, es encontrar soluciones. Hemos tenido lesiones, un inicio de Liga retrasado y 28 días sin jugar, pero sabíamos que tendríamos que afrontar estos desafíos. No estamos contentos con los últimos resultados, aunque también hemos hecho cosas muy buenas”. El regreso a San Mamés: “Estamos entre los cuatro mejores equipos en estadísticas como posesión, centros, disparos y llegadas al último tercio. Eso significa que no estamos tan lejos de volver a marcar goles”. El Getafe y sus dificultades: “Es un equipo muy bien organizado, que juega de manera directa, intensa y con mucha fortaleza. Hemos preparado lo que podemos esperar de ellos, pero hemos dedicado todavía más tiempo a corregir lo que no nos gustó de nuestro partido contra el Levante”. La falta de velocidad en ataque: “Necesitamos las dos cosas, velocidad y claridad. Cuando recuperamos el balón queremos aprovechar la oportunidad de atacar rápidamente, como hicimos contra el Atlético y el Celta. Pero cuando el rival no permite correr, necesitamos tener un buen juego posicional”. La polivalencia de Johaneko: “Puede jugar en las cuatro posiciones de banda, tanto de lateral como de extremo, por la derecha y por la izquierda. Contra el Elche vimos que generábamos mucho peligro con Nico Williams por la izquierda, pero nos faltaba por la derecha. Por eso decidimos utilizarle ahí. Está entrenando de manera increíble”. Alternativas a Guruzeta: “Esta temporada hemos utilizado a Iñaki, Guruzeta y Maroan como delanteros centro. También hemos probado a Robert Navarro como segundo delantero y sabemos que Nico Serrano ha jugado en esa posición. Estamos probando diferentes alternativas y entrenando con delanteros de la cantera. Necesitamos goles del nueve, pero no podemos limitarnos a exigirles que marquen”. Estado físico de Dani Vivian: “Cada día está más cerca de recuperar su nivel. Lo que vemos en los entrenamientos y los datos que manejamos son muy positivos. Parece preparado”. La recuperación de Beñat Prados: “Cada semana está más cerca, aunque hay mucha competencia en el centro del campo, con seis u ocho jugadores preparados para jugar. Está trabajando muy duro y cada día demuestra que se acerca el momento de volver a estar preparado para nosotros”.

articles.title: ​El Córdoba se regala un San Rafael feliz en seis minutos
articles.standfirst: Tras dos correcciones del VAR claves en la primera parte, Eder García y Diego Percan acaban con la resistencia de un Eibar atascado
articles.summary: Tras dos correcciones del VAR claves en la primera parte, Eder García y Diego Percan acaban con la resistencia de un Eibar atascado
articles.body: El Córdoba logró su objetivo de encadenar su segunda victoria consecutiva, a costa de la tercera jornada sin ganar de un Eibar a los que sus ocho cambios en el once no le funcionaron y que parece haberse atascado tras aquellas siete victorias seguidas. Tras una primera parte con dos correcciones claves del VAR, los blanquiverdes se regalaron con los tantos de Eder García y Diego Percan en apenas seis minutos el más feliz 24 de octubre, día de fiesta local por San Rafael y cumpleaños de su técnico Iván Ania, que cumplía 49 años. La primera parte, de dominio en general cordobesista, con casi una decena de saques de esquina y varias paradas de Jonmi Magunagoitia aunque en acciones no del todo claras -como un par a Carracedo y otra a Álex Martín-, estuvo marcada por dos correcciones del VAR. Primero, por un gol concedido a Javi Martón, tras aprovechar el rechace de Iker Álvarez a un remate de Gift, que acabó lesionado en dicha acción, que en realidad era fuera de juego. Y, ya en el añadido, cuando se quedó en amarilla un leve pisotón de Juan Gutiérrez a Guruzeta que el colegiado había castigado inicialmente con roja directa. Entre medias primero Tasende y después Percan, con todo a favor, no acertaron con la meta visitante. Esa supervivencia del Córdoba fue clave pues en la reanudación mostró la eficacia que le había faltado antes y en apenas seis minutos encarriló la victoria. Primero Eder García remató llegando desde atrás el buen centro de Adnane Ghailan y después Percan recibió en el área de Ghailan y marcó con un disparo raso y cruzado. Incluso poco después Carracedo pudo lograr el tercero con una volea desde la frontal pero Magunagoitia lo evitó con un auténtico paradón. Jokin Aranbarri tiró de titulares como Iván Gil o Jon Bautista, pero el Eibar apenas inquietó, salvo en un remate cercano de Jon Guruzeta que rechazó Rubén Alves. Incluso el Córdoba pudo hacer el tercero, pero Eder García se quedó sin doblete al estrellar un remate seco en el poste, ya dentro de un final plácido para los califales, que, en el añadido vieron cómo Magunagoitia volvía a aparecer ante Damián Cáceres y el propio Eder.

articles.title: El Elche ya suma más victorias y puntos a domicilio que en toda la temporada pasada
articles.standfirst: Con la goleada en Vallecas, los franjiverdes salen del descenso por primera vez desde agosto
articles.summary: Con la goleada en Vallecas, los franjiverdes salen del descenso por primera vez desde agosto
articles.body: El Elche va con la flecha hacia arriba. Ha pasado de un mal arranque a incluso ganar con brillantez. La goleada frente al Rayo Vallecano (0-3) ratifica su proyección, y le permite salir del descenso por primera vez desde agosto. Además, arroja numerosas estadísticas positivas: segunda victoria del curso; tercera portería a cero consecutiva; enlaza cuatro jornadas invicto, con ocho puntos de los doce últimos; y registra una única derrota en las seis últimas fechas ligueras. Todo ello, sustentado por un rendimiento como visitante de notable alto. Toda una antítesis respecto a la pasada campaña. Como clara muestra, este dato: sin haber acabado octubre, el equipo ilicitano ya suma más victorias y puntos a domicilio que en todo el último campeonato. Los hombres entrenados por Martín Anselmi han obtenido nueve puntos en seis salidas. El pasado curso, bajo el mando de Eder Sarabia, los franjiverdes sumaron ocho unidades en 19 partidos lejos del Martínez Valero. A nivel de victorias, el Elche actual lleva dos como foráneo, ante Espanyol (1-3) y Rayo Vallecano (0-3). En la temporada anterior, sólo ganó en el campo del colista, el Real Oviedo (1-2), un triunfo para el que hubo que esperar hasta finales de abril. Para más inri, los de Anselmi han puntuado en cinco de sus seis choques a domicilio. Con Sarabia, el conjunto ilicitano lo hizo en seis de 19. Este Elche puede considerarse una ‘rara avis’ en cierto modo, ya que no suele ser habitual que un equipo puntúe mucho más como visitante que como local. Nueve de sus diez puntos totales, es decir, el 90% de su puntaje, lo ha logrado en sus salidas. Venció a los citados Espanyol (1-3) y Rayo Vallecano (0-3) y empató en los territorios de Dépor (1-1), Athletic (1-1) y Villarreal (0-0), este último hace siete días. Sólo cayó frente al Racing (3-2). La altísima importancia de los guarismos a domicilio también se debe, en buena parte, al pobre nivel ofrecido por los franjiverdes en el Martínez Valero. Sólo han conseguido un punto de doce posibles en casa. Eso sí, lo extrajo en su último compromiso como anfitrión, ante el Celta (0-0). El Elche tratará de corregir su línea como local en su próxima cita. Tras dos salidas seguidas, recibirá al Valencia, en un duelo directo por la salvación. Antes, afrontará su partido de primera ronda de Copa del Rey, contra el Pinatar en tierras murcianas.

articles.title: Before Barcelona fame, Lamine Yamal’s childhood coach identified him as a ‘one in a million’ talent and drove him to training whenever his father couldn’t
articles.summary: Discover the incredible journey of Lamine Yamal, from a young child obsessed with football to a rising star at Barcelona and the Spanish national team. This article highlights the pivotal figures in his early life, including coaches and family, who played essential roles in nurturing his extraordinary talent.
articles.body: Long before Lamine Yamal became one of football’s most recognisable young stars, his journey depended on the people who recognised something extraordinary in a little boy who simply refused to leave the pitch. At La Torreta, where his childhood unfolded around a football, a handful of coaches witnessed the beginnings of a remarkable talent, while one of them occasionally drove him to training when his father could not, sharing Barcelona conversations with a boy destined to make history.The boy who wanted nothing except the ballInocente Diez, the youth coordinator at CF La Torreta, remembers an autumn afternoon when Mounir and Sheila brought their four-year-old son, Lamine Yamal, to the club, hoping to sign him up for football. Before the world knew his name, before Barcelona became the stage for his extraordinary rise, Diez had a simple task: put the little boy on the pitch and discover what happened when the game began.What followed offered an early glimpse into the mind of a child whose relationship with the ball seemed to leave little room for anything else. Diez recalled how some children cried, others played with the rubber pellets or the grass, and most found themselves distracted by something around them, whereas Yamal wanted the ball, took it from teammates and pursued goals with an intensity unusual for his age.“We put him on the pitch to see what he could do. Some kids cry, some start to play with the rubber pellets or the grass, most get distracted by something. All he wanted was the ball and he would even take it from his team-mates. He was obsessed with the ball and all he wanted to do was score goals. When training was over, he didn’t want to leave the pitch. We constantly had to tell him off because he never wanted to leave.”Diez understood that the distinction extended beyond enthusiasm, because the boy’s movements, positioning and understanding of football seemed remarkably developed for someone still learning how to navigate childhood. From the very first day, he considered Yamal “exceptional”, describing a player whose instincts made him stand apart from the other children, even before anyone could imagine the scale of his eventual achievements.“He was different to the others: the way he moved, the way he positioned himself, the way he understood the game, despite being so young. He is one of those people who’s been born under a lucky star: one in a million. It’s crazy,” said Diez.The journeys that mattered beyond the training groundThose early years at La Torreta also depended on practical kindness, the sort that rarely enters a footballer’s public biography but can quietly determine whether a child makes it onto the pitch. When Yamal’s father could not take him to training, Diez would collect him by car, helping the young player continue his footballing routine while his parents dealt with their work commitments.The distance between them in age was considerable, with approximately fifty years separating the experienced youth coordinator from the aspiring footballer in his passenger seat. Yet their conversations found common ground through the game itself, as they discussed football players and Barcelona’s results during drives that connected a small-town childhood with the club whose colours would eventually define Yamal’s professional career.There was something quietly fitting about those journeys, because Barcelona already occupied a place in the boy’s footballing imagination while the people around him worked to keep his development moving forward. Diez’s daughter also worked alongside Yamal’s mother at a fast-food restaurant, another connection between their families that placed the child’s ambitions within the everyday rhythms of work, responsibility and community.Yamal grew up in a humble family, and his progress required the combined efforts of parents, coaches and people willing to help when circumstances made the ordinary arrangements difficult. Before the extraordinary goals and record-breaking appearances, there were these unremarkable acts of support, repeated often enough to become part of the foundation beneath his rise.Leo Giordanella and the battle to teach a prodigy to passAnother important figure in Yamal’s earliest football education was Leo Giordanella, an Argentinian coach whose own journey to the touchline began far from the professional football spotlight. Born in Cipolletti, Patagonia, in 1992, Giordanella arrived in Barcelona with his family during the early 2000s, initially playing handball, the principal sport in Granollers, before moving into basketball and eventually football.His friends encouraged him to pursue the game after recognising his ability, and at fifteen or sixteen he joined CF La Torreta, where he subsequently received the opportunity to coach a youth team alongside his girlfriend. The coaches were still minors themselves, which meant Giordanella sometimes depended on his father or the parents of players for transport, before his girlfriend obtained her driving licence and the three of them began travelling to matches together with young Lamine.“We were minors ourselves, so my father or one of the players’ parents would drive us to training,” said Giordanella, who later worked as a lorry driver and remained a devoted football supporter.Giordanella first encountered Yamal through informal football in a park, where the boy’s father occasionally arrived with friends and brought his young son along. He remembered a small child with long, curly hair chasing a ball that seemed almost too large for him, an image that captured the simplicity of Yamal’s earliest footballing days.“My friends and I used to go play football in the park. By chance, Lamine’s father went with his friends to the same place and he sometimes brought Lamine. He was cute because he was this little kid with long curly hair running after the ball all day. The ball was bigger than him,” Giordanella told FIFA.Even at that age, Yamal appeared to possess technical instincts that did not require the usual patient introduction to the fundamentals. Giordanella remembered a youngster who could stop the ball, turn, perform step-overs and, by five or six, already score delicate chips over goalkeepers, making matches feel like performances in which he repeatedly became the central attraction.“He would stop the ball, turn, perform step-overs and at five or six years old, he was already scoring chips over goalkeepers. He stood out above the rest. Every match was a show.”For Giordanella, however, coaching the gifted youngster involved a persistent challenge, because Yamal's instinct was to keep the ball and solve situations himself rather than immediately involve his teammates. He benched him two or three times, only to watch him return and change the course of matches, a decision that later amused people who struggled to understand why a coach would leave such a talent out.Giordanella explained that the purpose was to encourage teamwork, reduce individualism and introduce the principles of tiki-taka, ensuring the youngster understood that football could demand collaboration as much as individual brilliance.From La Torreta to Barcelona, and towards a meeting with MessiDiez recognised the same tendency, tracing Yamal’s individualism to hours spent playing alone with his father’s dogs in the park or dribbling around dining-room chairs at home. Gradually, the child began to understand when passing could help his team, and Diez remembered how astonishing the results became once goals and assists started arriving together.“He was a bit individualistic because he was used to playing on his own with his father’s dogs in the park or dribbling around the dining-room chairs, but in the end, he understood that he had to pass. When he started to provide assists, it was completely insane. By the end of the game, he’d have scored several goals and provided several assists. Sometimes, he’d dribble past the goalkeeper and then pass the ball back for a team-mate to score.”In 2014, at seven years old, Yamal joined Barcelona’s youth academy after trying out with Espanyol and choosing the Catalan club instead. The decision began a journey that would eventually take him from La Torreta’s pitches to European football’s grandest stages, where he became a European champion at seventeen years and one day old and established himself as a leading figure for both Barcelona and Spain.By the time he turned nineteen, Yamal had already made history at both the European Championship and the FIFA World Cup, becoming a European champion at seventeen years and one day old before reaching the 2026 World Cup final with Spain. His achievements had established him among the defining young talents of international football, while the final against Argentina carried an especially personal connection through Lionel Messi, Yamal’s idol, whose own history with the youngster stretched back to a remarkable photograph taken in 2007.The image showed Messi, then nineteen, bathing a three-month-old Yamal, creating one of football’s most striking coincidences between two generations of extraordinary talent. Reflecting on the photograph ahead of the final at New York New Jersey Stadium, Messi remarked, “That photo is crazy,” before offering a wider appreciation of the young Spaniard’s achievements and future.“Lamine is a phenomenal player. I follow him closely because he plays for a club I love and I always wish him the best. He’s one of the best players in the world and he’s only 19. He has his whole career ahead of him and he has a great opportunity to make history,” Messi said on the eve of the final.The connection between Argentina and Yamal’s story reaches further back than that famous photograph, because his first trainer, Leo Giordanella, was himself an Argentinian who helped shape the young Spaniard’s earliest footballing years. With Yamal having now reached the FIFA World Cup™ final against Argentina, the occasion brought Giordanella’s loyalties into sharp focus, placing his affection for a former pupil alongside his enduring love for his homeland and Lionel Messi. “I have mixed feelings,” he admitted. “I’m Argentinian through and through and I love Messi, but I also have great affection for Lamine."Spain gave me a life, but I can’t forget where I was born and raised. I sent Lamine a message saying I love him very much but I love my country too and if he scores against Argentina, I’ll kill him,” he said jokingly.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Sheffield United 1-1 Derby: Patrick Bamford strikes to hold 10-man Rams
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Sheffield United and Derby County at Bramall Lane on Saturday; Patrick Bamford scores as Blades hit back after Dion Sanderson red card leaves Rams with 10 men.
articles.body:
Bobby Clark gave the visitors a first-half lead with Bamford levelling the scores late in the game, only to limp off amid the celebrations.

After a quiet start, the game burst into life around the half-hour mark with efforts on goal at either end.

Derby threatened when the ball fell to Clark following a cross from Joe Ward and his firm drive was well saved by Michael Cooper down to his right.

Carlton Morris then found himself through on goal and fired in a shot on target which was saved by Cooper with his legs.

United's first effort of note came from Kalvin Phillips, whose long-range strike forced a save from Jacob Widell Zetterstrom.

Derby took the lead in the 37th minute when Ryan Hedges, on the left-hand side of the area, saw his low shot come back off the near post and the ball fell to Clark, who fired into the net from inside the D.

Blades boss Chris Wilder made a double substitution shortly before the hour-mark, sending on Sydie Peck and Femi Sereki.

Ben Brereton Diaz put an effort off target for the hosts while Derby's Sammie Szmodics chested the ball down before volleying over.

The visitors were reduced to 10 men in the 66th minute when Dion Sanderson received a second booking following a clumsy challenge on Sereki.

After Romelle Donovan had an effort saved by Zetterstrom, the substitute played a key role in the equaliser.

The goal came in the 79th minute when Donovan delivered a probing cross to the far post and Bamford was on hand to bundle the ball over the line from close range. Bamford was injured in the process, however, after falling awkwardly and he had to be replaced.

Peck fired in a shot on target but it was straight at Zetterstrom who made a comfortable save.

Tyrese Campbell and fellow substitute Peck had chances to win it for the hosts in time added on.

Campbell saw his shot on the turn force a fine save from Zetterstrom, who turned the ball onto the bar and away, then Peck fired in a shot which the keeper was again equal to.

Donovan saw his shot comfortably saved and in the dying seconds of the game United skipper Japhet Tanganga put an effort straight at Zetterstrom.

The result means that Derby have won just once in their opening 12 games of the season.

"It was never going to be a straightforward game, as a Championship game never is. Really frustrated and disappointed with our first-half performance. I thought maybe the team thought that the game would come to them.

"It's always a full house when we go there and when they come to us, and it was always going to be competitive. And we gave them the game that they wanted first off, and that was down to us and our approach.

"We were too passive, we were too quick in possession, too slow in possession. We gave away the ball when we needed to have control, we went long when we needed to shorten things up.

"Out of possession, we lost too many first and second balls, and we never got up to the ball. It felt we needed a poke of some sort to get us going, which was annoying. And the poke came in the form of the goal.

"Everybody's brother was playing first half apart from Kalvin (Phillips) and Coops (Michael Cooper) and we turned up second half, tried to get back into the game.

"I've got to say, for the life of me, we have to win from that position. I thought the intent of the team was really good. Goalkeeper's made some huge saves for his team. A couple of things that could have fallen for us didn't."

Very proud of the effort of the group. I thought we were excellent in the first half. I thought we were fully in control of the game.

"We played some good football. We created a fantastic goal. And then in the second half, we knew we'd be under a bit of pressure. I felt we downlined that. And then just before the red card, we were again creating a few chances.

"Really disappointed not to get all three points of course but to go up against a really good, physical team that were going to put the ball in the box and sustain attacks. Overall I was really pleased with the way we defended.

"The fighting spirit was there for everyone to see. Over the course of the season up to now, we've had our so called better players not available. And, you know, the players that have performed have been excellent.

"Their attitude has been very good. We looked more of a physical presence, which we haven't in previous matches. It's about getting the group back together.

"I was really pleased and proud of the effort of the group, and you know, it just showed the togetherness of the group."

On the challenge that led to Sanderson's second booking, Eustace said: "I haven't seen it back but obviously if they're hunting a yellow card, it's the way the referee read the game today, he's probably always going to get another yellow so can't be doing it."

articles.title: Charlton 1-3 Norwich: Canaries hit back to end losing run
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Charlton Athletic and Norwich City at The Valley on Saturday; Canaries ease pressure on boss Philippe Clement with comeback win.
articles.body:
Charlie Kelman fired Charlton into an early lead but Paris Maghoma equalised for the Canaries, who then went ahead through Mathias Kvistgaarden and wrapped up victory via an Ivan Mesik own goal.

Charlton had a chance inside the opening 20 seconds but Tyreece Campbell was unable to beat City goalkeeper Daniel Grimshaw.

Norwich had the ball in the net in the fifth minute, Jack Stacey tucked away a reverse pass by captain Pelle Mattsson, but it was flagged for offside.

The Addicks started with real intensity, their press unsettling the Canaries, and it led to the opening goal on 10 minutes.

Kayne Ramsay nipped in to intercept Harry Darling's pass and Kelman, one of four changes made by Charlton boss Nathan Jones, took a touch on Joe Rankin-Costello's pass to go around Grimshaw and finish from a tight angle.

Billy Koumetio made a perfectly-timed tackle to dispossess Kvistgaarden in the penalty box in the 22nd minute.

Norwich finished the first period stronger as the hosts began to sit deeper.

A driving run from Maghoma, leaving Rankin-Costello trailing, saw the City attacker produce a low cross which narrowly evaded Kvistgaarden on the edge of the six-yard box.

Ramsay was at fault for the Norwich equaliser on 35 minutes. The Charlton right-back attempted a flick which was pounced on by Kvistgaarden and his threaded pass was dispatched impressively past Arthur Okonkwo by Maghoma as he opened his goal account for the campaign.

City finished the half controlling the ball and that continued after the action resumed.

Andre Brooks shot wide from a clear-cut opportunity before Kvistgaarden collected his third goal of the campaign, heading in from six yards out from Ruairi McConville's cross.

Charlton believed they had levelled in the 57th minute when McConville headed into his own net from Campbell's cross but it was struck off for offside.

Okonkwo came out quickly to smother a chance for Oscar Schwartau and then Grimshaw was equally quick to close the angle to frustrate Kelman shortly after the hour mark.

Norwich moved further ahead in the 75th minute as Mesik scored an own goal. Substitute Anthony Musaba's cross sliced off the Slovakian international and past Okonwko.

Charlton's keeper made two more saves to keep the margin of defeat down, tipping away Jacob Wright's shot and then saving from his legs as livewire Musaba tried to add a fourth.

It was the Addicks' first defeat at The Valley this season and they are now without a victory in nine Championship matches.

"We have to find a way to be more difficult to play against. Right now we are too easy and we concede goals too easily. That is a recipe for disaster in football.

"We started really well in the opening 20 minutes and had two or three chances. We took the lead and were playing exactly as I wanted us to play. With a little more guile we could have gone further ahead but we didn't punish them.

"When they had opportunities, a lot were gifted, we didn't do the basics well enough to stop that.

"It is just decision making. It is a poor pass that gifted them the ball to score but we don't handle the counter-attack well. Nobody closes down.

"The second goal is alarming because no-one goes to the ball, we allow him (Ruairi McConville) to deliver a flighty ball and we're all over the place as a back four.

"These things are costing us. A year ago we would have seen that game out."

"I really believe in the quality of this group. We could have had many more points than we have today and I'm fully confident in this group of players. They still need to learn a lot but that's normal with the ages we have.

"We went behind and the positive is that this group, I've been saying it for weeks, has a lot of desire to get results. They stay resilient and keep going. There has not been a game where they have given up or are not running. Those are the basics in the team - they are doing that.

"We took domination of the game. We scored three good goals and it could've been more. The defensive part was there, combined with the offensive part, for 70 minutes. The target for the next game is to do it for 90 minutes.

"We had difficulty with Charlton's shape for 15 or 20 minutes but, after that, we started to play our football."
