articles.title: Tottenham 1-2 Arsenal: Alessia Russo penalty gives Gunners north London derby win in WSL to ease pressure on Renée Slegers
articles.summary: Match report as Arsenal end their winless run with a 2-1 victory over Tottenham at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium; Georgia Stanway equalised after Cathinka Tandberg's opener before Russo scored from the penalty spot; Gunners up to sixth in the WSL
articles.body:
The Gunners had won only once in their opening six league games and started the weekend eighth, six points behind fourth-placed Spurs. They fell behind to Cathinka Tandberg's 13th-minute header but Georgia Stanway equalised four minutes later before Alessia Russo converted a second-half penalty.

Tottenham started brightly and exposed Arsenal's defensive weaknesses in transition, but their intensity faded as the first half progressed. Russo was denied by an outstanding Lize Kop save after the break before scoring from the spot in the 56th minute, after the ball struck substitute Ella Morris' outstretched hand during a scramble from a corner.

The penalty decision was a harsh one but Russo, who has missed some big chances in recent games, made no mistake to give Arsenal the lead.

Spurs pushed for an equaliser, with Shekiera Martinez having the ball in the net from close range in the 82nd minute, only for the offside flag to deny them. Arsenal held on for a much-needed win, offering some breathing room after a dismal start.

13: GOAL! Tandberg fires Tottenham ahead as Pelova's corner catches Arsenal out.

17: GOAL! Stanway levels for Arsenal with a powerful strike after Russo's pass.

50: Sombath is stretchered off following an injury, with Morris coming on for Tottenham.

54: WHAT A SAVE! Kop makes an outstanding one-on-one save to deny Russo after Foord pulls the ball back.

56: GOAL! Russo sends Kop the wrong way from the penalty spot to put Arsenal ahead after the ball strikes Morris' hand in the box.

Analysis: Did Arsenal just revive their season with derby win?

"Could this be the moment Arsenal's season finally takes off? A north London derby win might be exactly what Renée Slegers needed.

"Arsenal arrived at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium under real pressure, winless in five WSL games and with just five goals in six matches.

"Defeat would have intensified questions over Slegers' future. Instead, her side showed some much-needed resilience to come from behind and claim a huge three points.

"It wasn't perfect. Arsenal looked nervous early on, conceded from a corner and remained vulnerable in transition.

"But Georgia Stanway's response was emphatic, while Alessia Russo delivered the decisive moment from the penalty spot after being denied by Lize Kop moments earlier.

"The result will lift confidence, particularly for Russo, who has struggled for her usual clinical edge. A derby victory can change the mood around a club, and the travelling supporters made their relief clear.

"Now Arsenal must build on it. One win will not fix their season, but this could be the turning point Slegers desperately needed."

Arsenal head coach Renee Slegers speaking to BBC Sport:

"I'm happy because I see the fans and what it means for them. We were playing for the fans today. I'm happy for the players, who have stuck in during a really difficult period for us.

"I'm happy they have got the reward for all their work. There were good moments from us today. It was a step in the right direction and I'm very happy with the win, but now we have to back it up over the next couple of games.

"I think we were brave in our press and connected in those decisions. We did well playing around them, dominating the ball in phases and looking for the things that work for us.

"We created good opportunities, big opportunities, which I'm pleased with."

articles.summary: Otra victoria del equipo de Cesc Fàbregas, ahora en Serie A
articles.body: El Como sumó ante el Sassuolo (2-0) su tercer triunfo consecutivo en cuestión de siete días. Tras imponerse a Fiorentina y Manchester United, el equipo de Fàbregas resolvió en casa para auparse, de momento, a la cuarta plaza del 'Calcio', superando al Milan. Douvikas fue la estrella con un doblete decisivo. Tras una goleada histórica en Champions sobre el Manchester United, Fàbregas afrontaba el duelo ante el Sassuolo con rotaciones. Nombres como Nico Paz o Jacobo Ramón empezaban en el banquillo. Y al Como le faltó calidad en la recta final. El Sassuolo y Aquilani, Con Rafa Obrador titular y la apuesta por el cambio de portero con Turati, acertaron de inicio: el italiano sacó varias manos de mérito ante Douvikas y Caqueret. La más clara para los visitantes, un gol anulado a Bakola por fuera de juego previo de Bowie. A Da Cunha, en el Como, también le 'quitaron' un tanto. Sin embargo, todo cambió tras el descanso. Cesc reaccionó y metió en el campo a Jacobo Ramón, Addai y Luis Milla dentro al descanso. A los tres minutos ya ganaba 1-0 gracias a un tanto de Douvikas. El griego, poco después, hizo el segundo. El ex Celta acumula 25 tantos desde que arrancara la pasada temporada: solamente Lautaro y Malen mejoran sus números en Serie A. Impresionante. Tres puntos que permiten al Como seguir ascendiendo en la Serie A y dejar claro que, otro año más, serán un equipo candidato al top-4. Ya son cuartos.

articles.title: Kerala Blasters get Kochi stadium for ISL home matches at Rs 3.5 lakh per game
articles.summary: The Kerala government on Saturday allotted the Jawaharlal Nehru International Stadium in Kochi to Kerala Blasters FC for their home matches in the 2026-27
articles.body: The Kerala government on Saturday allotted the Jawaharlal Nehru International Stadium in Kochi to Kerala Blasters FC for their home matches in the 2026-27 Indian Super League (ISL) season at a rent of Rs 3.5 lakh per match.The order was issued by the Local Self Government Department a day before the Blasters are scheduled to host Mumbai City FC in their first home match of the season. The stadium is owned by the Greater Cochin Development Authority (GCDA).The government has also fixed a security deposit of Rs 25 lakh for the use of the stadium.In its order, the government said it had considered the club's request and recognised Kerala Blasters' role in the growth of football in the state and in encouraging youngsters to take an interest in sports.It also noted the contribution of the club and the ISL to the development of sports infrastructure in the state. Supporting Kerala Blasters, one of the state's prominent football clubs, was in the public interest, the order said.The Jawaharlal Nehru International Stadium has been Kerala Blasters' home ground since the ISL began in 2014.The Blasters will host Mumbai City FC on Sunday as they look to bounce back from a 4-1 defeat to NorthEast United FC. Mumbai City, meanwhile, will be chasing their first win of the season after collecting just one point from their opening two matches.Kerala head coach Ashley Westwood acknowledged the defensive mistakes that contributed to the defeat but said the team was still settling into the season. With limited time together during pre-season, the Blasters are working on building combinations and settling on a consistent starting eleven.Westwood, however, said his side would continue to play an attacking game."We try and play intense, aggressive football. articles.title: Anselmi: "Entendimos los momentos del partido, tanto en la previa como durante"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador del Elche celebra la victoria en Vallecas, que permite a su equipo salir del descenso: “Me genera deseo de seguir siendo mejores”
articles.summary: El entrenador del Elche celebra la victoria en Vallecas, que permite a su equipo salir del descenso: “Me genera deseo de seguir siendo mejores”
articles.body: El entrenador del Elche, Martín Anselmi, analizó el triunfo de su equipo frente al Rayo Vallecano (0-3). Una victoria que permite a los franjiverdes ampliar su buena línea y salir de la zona de descenso. Análisis: “Insistimos en ser un equipo inteligente, que entiende los momentos de los partidos, tanto en la previa como durante. Sabíamos que atacan vertical, con gente rápida. Entendíamos que estando juntos, sin saltar antes y que las profundidades no entren, y saliendo rápido a las transiciones, podíamos hacer daño. Y con el balón, estar tranquilos y ser nosotros. Hicimos un partido muy completo”. ¿Qué supone la victoria?: “Hay que seguir. La liga te invita a ello. Hay que preparar el partido del martes de Copa. Y después, el siguiente de liga. La única forma de jugar bien, ser lo que quieres como equipo y obtener victorias es trabajando. Me llena de orgullo cómo compiten los jugadores. Son muy valientes por hacerlo como hacen. En el descanso, hablamos de que queríamos mantener la portería a cero. No sé si el club ha logrado tres porterías a cero consecutivas. Tocaba defender y todos se entregan al máximo. Ser parte de un equipo a veces es hacer lo que no te gusta por el bien del equipo. Eso nos representa. Y cuando ganas, se subraya”. Claves de la eficacia: “No cambió nada, solo el tiempo. Cuando insistes y crees en el proceso, te salen las cosas mejor. No hay magia ni transformación extraña. Desde el partido en San Mamés, insistimos en esta forma de llegar al área. El trabajo te paga, y hp nos pagó”. Cambio de Gonzalo Villar: “Teníamos tres amonestados en el campo. Me parecían demasiados. Había que escoger. Y había gente como Facu (Buonanotte) que merecían jugar”. Cambio de Fer Niño: “Tenía un problema en la lumbar, ya antes del partido, y se le cargó. Le cambiamos por precaución”. Fede Redondo: “Hizo un partido de diez, con gol incluido”. Más puntos a domicilio que la temporada pasada: “Cuando llegamos al club, nuestro mensaje más contundente era ser un equipo. Eso lo heredamos. El segundo era invitarles a ser mejores. Lo exponemos todos los días. Ese es nuestro objetivo. Y la única manera de capitalizarlo es con puntos. Esto significa que estamos siendo mejores como visitantes. Ahora toca hacerlo en casa”. Tendencia positiva: “La futurología no va conmigo. Martes en Copa y domingo el Valencia. Ese es el mensaje”. Afición: “Ser hincha es seguir el corazón. Y a veces, no entiende de razones, sino de pasiones. Cuando te dejas llevar con el corazón cuando es tu equipo, vas. Y en el campo, nos toca representarles. Hoy, fue el combo perfecto”. Ambiente en Vallecas: “Cuando queremos dedicarnos al fútbol, es para estar en escenarios donde la gente se hace sentir. Más allá de que el fondo no estaba habilitado, la hinchada del Rayo se hizo sentir. Pero para mí, lo de afuera no cuenta. Los jugadores son los que juegan. Lo demás, es ruido. Tratamos de aislarnos”. Fuera del descenso: “Es más lindo verse ahí. Pero para seguir estando ahí, hay que seguir. Me genera deseo de seguir siendo mejores”.

articles.title: Aston Villa 2-1 Man City: Gianluigi Donnarumma and Marc Guehi under spotlight
articles.summary: Manchester City's 100% winning start to the Premier League season comes to an abrupt end against Aston Villa - leaving Enzo Maresca with glaring defensive issues to resolve.
articles.body:
Manchester City 's 100% winning start to the Premier League season came to an abrupt end against Aston Villa - leaving Enzo Maresca with glaring defensive issues to resolve.

Nicolas Jackson's double in a 2-1 home win for Villa means City have now managed only one clean sheet in their past six games and the form of goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma and defender Marc Guehi is of concern.

Since the start of last season, only eight players have made more errors leading to Premier League goals than Donnarumma and Guehi with three each.

City's most recent shutout came in their impressive victory at Liverpool two weeks ago but, around that game, City have conceded against teams ranging from Champions League holders Paris St-Germain to top-flight strugglers Sunderland .

Maresca was forced to try different combinations at the back against Villa, but as the legendary Sir Alex Ferguson once said, "attack wins you games, defence wins you titles".

Though still early days in the campaign and guaranteed to be in the top two come the end of the weekend, City need to shore up their backline if they are to stay there.

Asked if the two goals were avoidable, Maresca told TNT Sports: "Absolutely, both.

"Sometimes you have to be a bit more lucky because we only conceded those two chances, but we created a lot of chances.

"We played most of the game in their box but you have to be clinical and avoid mistakes like the two goals we conceded."

Jackson stars with two goals - player ratings for Aston Villa v Man City

Jackson double for Villa ends Man City's 100% start

Donnarumma 'could have done better' for second goal

City were undone by goals in each half from the brilliant Jackson at a raucous Villa Park to end their streak of seven straight wins at the start of this campaign.

Maresca's team started the season by conceding eight goals in their first nine games but that has seen a dramatic downturn, with nine goals hitting the back of their net in the past four matches.

The signing of Donnarumma last summer was heralded as the acquisition of one of the best goalkeepers in the world to replace Ederson.

The Brazilian changed the face of English football with his footwork, spraying short and long passes across the pitch, and there are few keepers who can come close to matching that.

But Italy captain Donnarumma struggles with the ball at his feet and often puts his team-mates in trouble with passes out from the back.

On Saturday, City captain Ruben Dias gesticulated to his team-mate to send the ball up the pitch after the Portuguese failed to control a difficult pass.

Maresca decided to sell James Trafford to Leeds for £45m in the summer, and the England international has been impressive at Elland Road.

Trafford has made more passes than Donnarumma this season, has a slightly better rate at preventing goals and has come out to sweep the ball 11 times compared with Donnarumma's one.

Though Donnarumma could do little about Jackson's thumping finish for the opening goal, he should have done better for the second as a low shot seemed to squirm under him.

Former City defender Steph Houghton said on BBC Radio 5 Live: "I think Villa really utilised keeping the ball and being a real threat to Manchester City . Donnarumma, especially with the second goal, could probably have done a little bit better.

"But I don't want to take anything away from Villa. I think they performed really, really well and the gameplan was spot on, just to nullify City as much as possible."

Centre-back Guehi's £20m arrival from Crystal Palace in January was considered a bargain.

But it was his loose pass at Everton late last season which cost City dearly in the title race, drawing that game and losing the impetus to eventual champions Arsenal .

This season has been a struggle for the England defender, culpable for both goals scored by Ipswich last weekend and being picked off by John McGinn deep in his own half for Villa's first goal.

Later in the half, he hauled down Jackson on the edge of the box before being shown a yellow card, and was put out of his misery by being taken off at half-time.

City sources had said they were targeting signing a right-back in the summer before pivoting elsewhere, saying Abdukodir Khusanov can provide back-up should Matheus Nunes not be available.

Khusanov started out wide but struggled before being moved inside in place of Guehi, while Rico Lewis was brought to fill the gap, with Maresca acknowledging afterwards he needs to "find that balance" in defence.

Villa supporters provided constant reminders to the travelling fans of their side being "cheats", and the vitriol faced following the guilty verdict of the financial charges may be beginning to weigh on the players' minds.

Asked by BBC Sport if Guehi's form is a worry, Maresca said: "No, I'm not worried about Marc at all.

"I know he is playing every minute since the season started with us and the national team, so it's not easy but the change was also because he was on a yellow card.

"The way we want to be aggressive sometimes, to have one yellow card can be dangerous but I am not worried at all."

Maresca, though, should be concerned by coming up against Fabian Hurzeler's free-scoring Brighton twice next week - in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday, and Premier League on Saturday.

The Italian needs to fix the defensive leaks before they become something more serious.

articles.summary: El partido pudo disputarse con normalidad tras lo sucedido ante el Athletic hace dos semanas
articles.body: La tarde en Vallecas comenzó con la firme atención a lo que pudiese suceder en la grada después de lo que aconteció ante el Athletic hace dos semanas y tras lo que el partido ante los vascos tuvo que suspenderse. El viernes por la noche, y tras anunciar el club la devolución del importe de abonos por los tres partidos jugados fuera de su estadio, las peñas ya dejaron caer un 'alto el fuego'.

articles.title: Beñat San José: "La afición ha estado de 10 y faltaba la grada de animación"
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Rayo analizó la derrota frente al Elche
articles.summary: El técnico del Rayo analizó la derrota frente al Elche
articles.body: El Rayo volvió a disputar los 90 minutos de fútbol en Vallecas y acabó siendo derrotado. El Elche, con los goles de Redondo y de Fer Niño en la primera parte y de Valera en la segunda, provocó el primer descalabro del cuadro franjirrojo como local de la temporada. Beñat San José atendió a los medios de comunicación tras el duelo. Declaraciones de Lejeune ("nos han pintado la cara"): "No comparto, pero entiendo que los jugadores están calientes. Hemos tenido nuestras oportunidades, la primera parte ha sido de tú a tú. Hemos hecho una presión alta y su portero nos ha puesto en un aprieto con el juego en largo. Hemos tenido ocasiones, acercamientos. Han venido esos dos penaltis y hemos recibido dos goles y es muy duro. No me han parecido tan claros. Hemos tenido chances para crear peligro en la primera parte. No es cuestión de 'pintar la cara' es cuestión de que hoy no nos ha salido nada y a ellos todo". Cambios de Camello y De Frutos: "Camello tenía unas molestias en los isquios y Jorge ha tenido unos problemas gástricos durante toda la semana. Nos hemos dado cuenta de que necesitábamos refrescar". Fondo vacío: "Nosotros queremos un estadio lleno, la parte de animación la hemos echado muchísimo de menos, nos hubiese gustado que hubieran estado". Pathé Ciss como lanzador del penalti: "Hay una lista de lanzadores y son ellos los que lo deciden. Pathé es uno de ellos". Penaltis: "Si no los ha pitado es porque no han sido y no voy a hacer ninguna crítica. Sobre todo el primero no nos ha parecido". Preparación del partido: "Esta semana ha sido especialmente difícil porque no sólo nos hemos dedicado a entrenar, sino también a reunirnos. Es necesario. No es ninguna excusa para el partido de hoy. Lástima que no hayamos podido ofrecer el mejor partido a los aficionados". ¿Cómo está?: "Muy orgulloso de ser entrenador del Rayo y de representar a este club, este barrio, esta afición y estos jugadores. No estoy feliz, pero sí de ser el entrenador de este hermoso estadio y de todo lo que conlleve el club, que es muy especial. Hoy hemos tenido un día malo y estamos fastidiados". Aviso de lo que venía: "Me han dicho todos los hándicaps e inconvenientes. Este inicio de temporada todo ha explotado, el vaso rebosa y me ha tocado vivir una situación que hasta entonces ningún entrenador ha vivido como tal. Además de lo malo, también te puedo decir lo bueno. La afición ha estado de 10 y faltaba la grada de animación".

articles.title: Orian Goren, la última perla de La Masia, mira al Clásico
articles.standfirst: El mediocentro podría ser la principal novedad en la convocatoria culé
articles.summary: El mediocentro podría ser la principal novedad en la convocatoria culé
articles.body: Orian Goren apunta a ser la principal novedad en la lista de convocados que Hansi Flick anunciará mañana domingo. Si entra, el joven centrocampista se estrenará en una convocatoria en el encuentro más mediático de LaLiga: el Clásico. Flick conoce bien al mediocentro israelí, que participó en la pretemporada del primer equipo del Barcelona, incluido el Trofeo Joan Gamper. Durante esas semanas, Goren tuvo la oportunidad de trabajar junto a los futbolistas de la primera plantilla. Ahora, su más que posible presencia en la convocatoria representará un nuevo paso en su evolución. El mediocentro se ejercitó viernes y sábado a las órdenes del preparador alemán. Nacido en 2009, el centrocampista se ha convertido en una pieza clave del Barça Atlètic, donde destaca por su continuidad en la medular. Es un fijo en el once. De hecho, su única ausencia fue por culpa de los compromisos internacionales, ya que durante el último parón fue convocado por la selección sub-21 de Israel, pese a tener tan solo 17 años. La inclusión de Goren en la lista del primer equipo llegaría condicionada por la baja por lesión de Dani Olmo. La trayectoria de Goren en el Barcelona comenzó en 2023, cuando aterrizó en La Masia procedente del Maccabi Petah de Israel. Tras consolidarse en el juvenil, esta campaña ha dado el salto al filial azulgrana. Su posible convocatoria para el Clásico supondría un nuevo capítulo en su progresión. A sus 17 años, Goren está ante una gran oportunidad de ir citado en el partido que todos sueñan en jugar. A ver mañana la lista de Hansi Flick.

articles.title: Ex-Middlesbrough star Emmanuel Latte Lath flags Michael Carrick concern amid Man United woes
articles.summary: Former Middlesbrough striker Emmanuel Latte Lath has revealed a Michael Carrick concern as the coach battles to keep his Manchester United job.Under pressure...
articles.body:
Former Middlesbrough striker Emmanuel Latte Lath has revealed a Michael Carrick concern as the coach battles to keep his Manchester United job.

Carrick is under immense pressure owing to United's awful start to the new season. United lie in the bottom half of the Premier League table, having managed just seven points from their opening seven games.

United have also been beaten in their last two Champions League games, including Wednesday's embarrassing 4-1 thrashing at the hands of Como.

Although results have been disappointing, the team's performances have been of even greater concern. Opposition sides have penetrated United at will, and the players appear incapable of competing physically.

Carrick is set to be in charge for Sunday's meeting with Bournemouth, with United insisting that it is business as usual. However, it feels like only a matter of time until a change is made in the dugout.

Links to the likes of Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann, Antonio Conte and Fabian Hurzeler have intensified over the past few days. Jason Wilcox is leaning more towards hiring Howe, while Christopher Vivell is pushing for Nagelsmann's appointment. A report covered by The Peoples Person relayed that tensions are rising between the two executives.

In his pre-match press conference ahead of the Bournemouth match, Carrick made an emotional statement to reporters, emphasising his care for the club and restating his belief that he is the right person for the role. Carrick recognised that he and his players are not meeting expectations and affirmed that they will make every possible effort to make amends.

Emmanuel Latte Lath, who worked with Carrick at Middlesbrough, spoke to the BBC and explained that Carrick could be too calm at times.

Latte Lath joined Middlesbrough in 2023 from Serie A outfit Atalanta. He was sensational in his debut campaign, netting 16 goals in 30 games.

But it was not enough as Carrick's side missed out on the Championship play-offs. During his second and final season, Latte Lath scored 11 goals by the early part of the new year, before opting to depart the Riverside Stadium and make the switch to MLS.

He is now on loan at Union Berlin in the Bundesliga.

Latte Lath told the BBC, "I found a good coach and a good person. It gave me straight away confidence."

"He was a calm person, a calm coach, maybe sometimes too much, but it was needed for us. He knew always when and what he should say to you in the difficult moment or in the good moment."

"So for me, I think in that point of my life, it was really important."

Michael Carrick vs. Bournemouth kicks off at 3 pm.

articles.title: Romano: ‘Liverpool tried’ to sign Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, but this is why PSG won the race instead
articles.summary: Fabrizio Romano has claimed that Liverpool ‘tried’ hard to sign Khvicha Kvaratskhelia from Napoli at the start of 2025, only for the winger to join Paris Sai...
articles.body:
Fabrizio Romano has claimed that Liverpool 'tried' hard to sign Khvicha Kvaratskhelia from Napoli at the start of 2025, only for the winger to join Paris Saint-Germain instead.

The Reds had been strongly linked with a potential swoop for the Georgia international midway through the 2024/25 season, but instead it was Luis Enrique's side who emerged triumphant in the transfer race.

The 25-year-old has won the Champions League twice in his 21 months in the French capital thus far, with PSG eliminating the Merseysiders on the way to both of those trophy wins, but he could very easily have ended up in red rather than navy in those clashes.

Romano: Liverpool 'tried' to sign Kvaratskhelia

Romano has detailed to DAZN how Liverpool pushed hard for Kvaratskhelia's signature, but ultimately the player was swayed by the 'very ambitious project' at the Parc des Princes.

The transfer reporter said: "Kvara has won an incredible amount of awards at Paris Saint-Germain, but remember, it was nearly Liverpool and not Paris [who he joined].

"An inside story from January 2025, when Kvaratskhelia decided to leave Napoli, to try something new, and from Premier League there were aggressive teams really keen on signing him.

(Photo by Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images)

"Chelsea were calling, but was not possible to make the deal happen. Chelsea were even prepared to include Mykhailo Mudryk in the negotiation with Napoli. Liverpool were also trying. Liverpool [were] very keen on Kvaratskhelia, but the player decided to go to PSG.

"PSG presented a very ambitious project and that was very smart from PSG to sign Kvaratskhelia and for Kvara to move to Paris, but Liverpool were really there. Liverpool tried, but it was not possible to proceed."

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Was Kvaratskhelia one that got away for Liverpool?

Could the Reds' fortunes since the start of 2025 have been different if Kvaratskhelia had chosen them and not Enrique's side?

It's purely hypothetical as to whether him joining Liverpool rather than PSG would've tipped the scales in our favour in the two Champions League knockout ties since his exit from Napoli, but it's not hard to imagine that he could've been the difference maker for the Reds in the round-of-16 tie the season before last which ended up in a penalty shootout.

Arne Slot's LFC managed just fine initially with Luis Diaz and Cody Gakpo vying for the left-sided attacking berth, but the Colombian's exit to Bayern Munich and the Dutchman's loss of form in 2025/26 may well have had Kopites regretting how the Kvaratskhelia pursuit ended up.

The Georgian has gone on to score 29 goals and set up another 20 in 91 games for PSG, but he won't be adding to any of those tallies for a long time after rupturing his ACL in his team's win over Barcelona earlier this week.

Liverpool fans might be wondering what could've been with the 25-year-old, but Andoni Iraola now has a plethora of left-sided attacking options in Gakpo, Rio Ngumoha, Victor Munoz and Kvaratskhelia's former teammate Bradley Barcola.

It wasn't to be with the Georgia international, but the Reds needn't have any regrets, for it seems that they at least threw everything they had at trying to get him to Anfield.

articles.summary: Max Allegri insists he didn’t ‘need to convince Kevin De Bruyne’ to be a deep playmaker for Napoli against Roma. ‘I just told him that was where he was playi...
articles.body:
Max Allegri insists he didn't 'need to convince Kevin De Bruyne' to be a deep playmaker for Napoli against Roma. 'I just told him that was where he was playing.'

It kicks off at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona at 17.00 UK time (18.00 CEST).

FLORENCE, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 20: Massimiliano Allegri manager of SSC Napoli looks on during the Serie A match between ACF Fiorentina and SSC Napoli at Stadio Artemio Franchi on September 20, 2026 in Florence, Italy. (Photo by Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Images)

Amir Rrahmani has been struggling with flu symptoms in recent days and is not even on the bench, while Antonio Vergara returns to the squad after his injury on international duty.

Alisson Santos, David Neres, Costantino Favasuli and Alessandro Buongiorno are long-term absentees.

This is the first time in Serie A this season that Kevin De Bruyne and Scott McTominay have started together , with the Belgium international again used as a playmaker, a role he does not seem enthusiastic about.

NAPLES, ITALY – OCTOBER 20: Massimiliano Allegri, Manager of SSC Napoli, waves to the camera before the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between SSC Napoli and FK Bodo/Glimt at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on October 20, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images)

"I put three in midfield and they are free to play," Allegri told DAZN Italia.

How did he convince De Bruyne to keep playing in such a deep playmaker role when the former Manchester City midfielder insisted he prefers being a trequartista?

"I didn't need to convince him, I just told him that was where he was playing, he knows how to move. Anguissa provides greater balance, while McTominay is certainly a more attack-minded player than the other two," insisted Allegri.

NAPLES, ITALY – OCTOBER 10: Kevin De Bruyne of SSC Napoli celebrates scoring his team's third goal during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and Frosinone Calcio at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on October 10, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images)

The mood in the Partenopei camp remains tense despite the 4-3 Champions League victory over Bodo/Glimt, because they are still playing catch-up in Serie A.

Last week they suffered a shock 3-1 defeat to rock bottom Venezia, prompting some debate over the future of the coach.

NAPLES, ITALY – OCTOBER 20: Massimiliano Allegri, Manager of SSC Napoli, reacts during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between SSC Napoli and FK Bodo/Glimt at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on October 20, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images)

"These are details that make the difference, so if you are not determined to close down players for the pass, the cross or the shot, you will have more difficulty. I got the feeling against Bodo/Glimt that we could concede at any moment, and were too sluggish," added Allegri.

"We are coming off a defeat to Venezia that interrupted our three-match unbeaten run. We've got to get back on track against a strong Roma side that is doing well, it is without doubt going to be an entertaining match that isn't over until it's over."

articles.title: Arsenal relieve pressure with Spurs win - can they kick on now?
articles.summary: Arsenal end their five-match winless run in the Women's Super League with victory at Tottenham - but can they kick on now?
articles.body:
Arsenal's victory over Tottenham on Saturday meant more than usual.

It was not just a win against their rivals at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, but a first in six Women's Super League matches and a huge release of pressure.

Upon hearing the final whistle, confirming their 2-1 success , Arsenal's players ran towards their supporters in the away end to celebrate passionately.

It was a visible show of emotion, a moment of relief and a sense things could finally be turning in their favour after a disappointing WSL start where they had beaten only Brighton.

Could it now be the catalyst to repair a campaign that looked to have been derailed in just two months.

Arsenal started the day in the bottom half of the table, four points off fourth-placed Tottenham and 12 points behind leaders Manchester City.

With their title ambitions in ruins, manager Renee Slegers was facing weekly questions about her future and defeat by Spurs could have been the last straw.

Confidence was at an all-time low and a high-stakes north London derby was not the ideal game to go into with no momentum.

The nerves were obvious as there were misplaced passes, poor clearances and sloppy errors in a disjointed first half.

Tottenham had even taken the lead, although they held it for just four minutes as Georgia Stanway's powerful strike cancelled out a header from Cathinka Tandberg.

When asked what she said to the players at half-time, boss Slegers revealed: "I just gave constructive and tactical things that could help us to get the win, and remind us about the fight and intensity on the pitch.

"It was a real derby. The team were in a good place and were finding solutions themselves. It was just constructive messaging."

Arsenal were much better in the second half, putting more pressure on Tottenham and getting the winning goal they needed.

Referee Phoebe Cross pointed to the spot when Lisa Baum's shot bounced off the post and Tandberg's clearance hit the outstretched hand of her Spurs team-mate Ella Morris nearby.

Alessia Russo, who had failed to convert a big chance just moments earlier, made no mistake the second time around and slotted the ball past goalkeeper Lize Kop.

She roared in celebration and sprinted towards the away fans - an outburst of emotion that was replicated at full-time by England team-mate Leah Williamson.

Slegers stood back as her players enjoyed the adulation from supporters. They had finally delivered a win and the fans had something to sing about.

"I'm so happy we got it for them. We said we would play for the fans. We played for them and connected with them," said Slegers.

"We sold out the away section, they came in the rain and sang and fought with us throughout the game.

"At the end, it was scrappy and it was game management and they were all there with us.

"You could see how the team responded and how they were with the fans. It was pure joy and happiness. We want to capitalise on these emotions."

It was the perfect result, but never easy.

Former Arsenal defender Gilly Flaherty told BBC One the visitors were "causing their own problems" in an unconvincing first half and they took time to settle.

They showed nervousness and had to cling on at the end, relying on a stroke of luck and a controversial refereeing decision to get them over the line.

But it was not undeserved and Slegers made the decision at full-time to show their feelings and celebrate with supporters in a different way, having abandoned their familiar post-match team huddle in the centre of the pitch.

"The fans were on our minds. We wanted to play for something bigger, not only for ourselves. That is always a balance," she said.

One Gunners fan told BBC Sport at half-time: "It's 1-1 but Arsenal look very nervy in and out of possession. Another week, another formation, another different starting XI. All feels so desperate and out of control."

Slegers showed understanding of their frustration as she added: "We normally do a huddle on the pitch but we decided to just go to the fans instead.

"Actions speak louder than words. There was not much more talking to do so we just wanted to celebrate with them.

"We had a run of games where results haven't been good enough. It was frustrating for everyone. This will definitely energise us."

Slegers is pleased Arsenal are set to embark on a busy period with their next game in the Women's Champions League on Wednesday against Benfica.

They have four home games in November and a trip to Barcelona - all good opportunities to build momentum.

Their WSL title hopes may be gone, but a top-three finish is imperative to secure European football next season.

"We need to back this up in the next couple of games. There were some really good things for us on the pitch," said Slegers.

"We want to be more consistent but this was a really good step. It's positive energy we want to capitalise on, but it's only a step."

articles.title: Man City's leaky defence highlights Donnarumma & Guehi struggles
articles.summary: Manchester City's 100% winning start to the Premier League season comes to an abrupt end against Aston Villa - leaving Enzo Maresca with glaring defensive is...
articles.body:
Manchester City's 100% winning start to the Premier League season came to an abrupt end against Aston Villa - leaving Enzo Maresca with glaring defensive issues to resolve.

Nicolas Jackson's double in a 2-1 home win for Villa means City have now managed only one clean sheet in their past six games and the form of goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma and defender Marc Guehi is of concern.

Since the start of last season, only eight players have made more errors leading to Premier League goals than Donnarumma and Guehi with three each.

City's most recent shutout came in their impressive victory at Liverpool two weeks ago but, around that game, City have conceded against teams ranging from Champions League holders Paris St-Germain to top-flight strugglers Sunderland.

Maresca was forced to try different combinations at the back against Villa, but as the legendary Sir Alex Ferguson once said, "attack wins you games, defence wins you titles".

Though still early days in the campaign and guaranteed to be in the top two come the end of the weekend, City need to shore up their backline if they are to stay there.

Asked if the two goals were avoidable, Maresca told TNT Sports: "Absolutely, both.

"Sometimes you have to be a bit more lucky because we only conceded those two chances, but we created a lot of chances.

"We played most of the game in their box but you have to be clinical and avoid mistakes like the two goals we conceded."

Donnarumma 'could have done better' for second goal

City were undone by goals in each half from the brilliant Jackson at a raucous Villa Park to end their streak of seven straight wins at the start of this campaign.

Maresca's team started the season by conceding eight goals in their first nine games but that has seen a dramatic downturn, with nine goals hitting the back of their net in the past four matches.

The signing of Donnarumma last summer was heralded as the acquisition of one of the best goalkeepers in the world to replace Ederson.

The Brazilian changed the face of English football with his footwork, spraying short and long passes across the pitch, and there are few keepers who can come close to matching that.

But Italy captain Donnarumma struggles with the ball at his feet and often puts his team-mates in trouble with passes out from the back.

On Saturday, City captain Ruben Dias gesticulated to his team-mate to send the ball up the pitch after the Portuguese failed to control a difficult pass.

Maresca decided to sell James Trafford to Leeds for £45m in the summer, and the England international has been impressive at Elland Road.

Trafford has made more passes than Donnarumma this season, has a slightly better rate at preventing goals and has come out to sweep the ball 11 times compared with Donnarumma's one.

Though Donnarumma could do little about Jackson's thumping finish for the opening goal, he should have done better for the second as a low shot seemed to squirm under him.

Former City defender Steph Houghton said on BBC Radio 5 Live: "I think Villa really utilised keeping the ball and being a real threat to Manchester City. Donnarumma, especially with the second goal, could probably have done a little bit better.

"But I don't want to take anything away from Villa. I think they performed really, really well and the gameplan was spot on, just to nullify City as much as possible."

Centre-back Guehi's £20m arrival from Crystal Palace in January was considered a bargain.

But it was his loose pass at Everton late last season which cost City dearly in the title race, drawing that game and losing the impetus to eventual champions Arsenal.

This season has been a struggle for the England defender, culpable for both goals scored by Ipswich last weekend and being picked off by John McGinn deep in his own half for Villa's first goal.

Later in the half, he hauled down Jackson on the edge of the box before being shown a yellow card, and was put out of his misery by being taken off at half-time.

City sources had said they were targeting signing a right-back in the summer before pivoting elsewhere, saying Abdukodir Khusanov can provide back-up should Matheus Nunes not be available.

Khusanov started out wide but struggled before being moved inside in place of Guehi, while Rico Lewis was brought to fill the gap, with Maresca acknowledging afterwards he needs to "find that balance" in defence.

Villa supporters provided constant reminders to the travelling fans of their side being "cheats", and the vitriol faced following the guilty verdict of the financial charges may be beginning to weigh on the players' minds.

Asked by BBC Sport if Guehi's form is a worry, Maresca said: "No, I'm not worried about Marc at all.

"I know he is playing every minute since the season started with us and the national team, so it's not easy but the change was also because he was on a yellow card.

"The way we want to be aggressive sometimes, to have one yellow card can be dangerous but I am not worried at all."

Maresca, though, should be concerned by coming up against Fabian Hurzeler's free-scoring Brighton twice next week - in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday, and Premier League on Saturday.

The Italian needs to fix the defensive leaks before they become something more serious.
authors: Shamoon Hafez - Manchester City reporter at Villa Park

articles.title: El Arsenal recupera su idilio con el balón parado y se sube al coliderato de la Premier
articles.standfirst: Konsa 'abrió la lata' a la salida de un córner en los primeros compases y Gabriel ratificó el triunfo ante el Everton mediada en la segunda parte para igualar en lo más alto con el City
articles.summary: Konsa 'abrió la lata' a la salida de un córner en los primeros compases y Gabriel ratificó el triunfo ante el Everton mediada en la segunda parte para igualar en lo más alto con el City
articles.body: El Arsenal había hecho del balón parado su mayor aliado. El curso pasado, sin contar penaltis, marcaron hasta 25 goles. En el presente, todavía no se habían estrenado. Pero, por medio de Konsa en los primeros instantes, la pizarra de Jover volvió a sonreírle a unos 'gunners' que se impusieron al Everton (2-0) para recuperar el coliderato de la Premier junto al Manchester City. Gabriel ratificó el triunfo mediada la segunda parte. Se especulaba con que Dowman, ante la lesión de un Bukayo Saka que podría estar varios meses fuera, partiese de inicio en la banda derecha del Arsenal. Arteta, sin embargo, desplazó a Madueke para darle una nueva oportunidad a Eze. Gyökeres —primera titularidad en Premier— les acompañaba arriba. Con Lewis-Skelly de vuelta al lateral izquierdo, fue Merino quien escoltó a Rice en el doble pivote. Se le venían atragantando al Arsenal los inicios de partido tras la vuelta del parón. La intención de salida, sin embargo, fue radicalmente opuesta a la de las últimas semanas y, poco después de que se cumpliesen los cinco primeros minutos de encuentro, recuperaron su idilio con el balón parado para ponerse por delante. Estuvo atento Konsa para recoger el 'cabezazo' de Gabriel al larguero que el Everton no acertó a despejar. Al Arsenal le entró la tentación de cederle ligeramente la iniciativa a los 'toffees'. Raya, en dos tiempos, repelió un remate mordido de Garner y, poco después, White tocó lo justo para desviar otro disparo con 'veneno' de Tyrique George. Los 'gunners' recuperaron el control y disfrutaron de varias ocasiones para duplicar la renta antes de poner rumbo al túnel de vestuarios. Estuvo magnífico Tarkowski defendiendo el área para frustrar a un Mikel Merino que volvió a tener la última a balón parado. El segundo acto arrancó bastante atropellado para el Arsenal. Raya, de hecho, siguió con la mirada un centro 'envenenado' a cargo de Röhl y, posteriormente, descolgó otro de Tyrique George. El Emirates, eso sí, se echó a temblar cuando, en su intento por cortar un envío lateral, Gabriel se quedó tendido en el suelo y solicitó asistencia médica. Se preparaba Mosquera para salir. El central brasileño, sin embargo, aguantó sobre el césped y, tras el triple cambio —Calafiori, Bruno Guimaraes y Havertz— que introdujo Arteta en el 66', fue el encargado de anotar el gol de la tranquilidad. Ben White rompió a línea de fondo, levantó la cabeza y puso un centro 'tocadito' que el ex del Lille se encargó de cabecear en el segundo palo. Arteta reclamó los servicios de Zubimendi, que acabó con la nariz rota, y el joven Dowman para cerrar un encuentro al que Dewsbury-Hall, anticipándose a Konsa y Gabriel cabeceando un centro de Garner, pudo darle vida durante los últimos minutos. El Arsenal, sin embargo, volvió a dejar su portería a cero —quinta en esta Premier— para igualar a un Manchester City que se mantiene por delante por diferencia de goles (+3).

articles.title: Bobb saca al Fulham de Arbeloa del descenso
articles.standfirst: Un golazo del noruego entregó la victoria a los 'Cottagers'
articles.summary: Un golazo del noruego entregó la victoria a los 'Cottagers'
articles.body: Dos victorias consecutivas y el Fulham se dispara al 12º puesto de la Premier League. El equipo de Álvaro Arbeloa, que no había ganado hasta la pasada jornada en liga, se impuso 0-1 al Coventry City con un solitario gol (y qué gol) de Oscar Bobb para salir del descenso... por fin. Fue un partido discreto, sin demasiado fútbol... pero con mucho en juego para ambos equipos. En el Fulham, solamente Gonzalo era titular mientras César Palacios y Manuel Ángel esperaban su turno desde el banquillo. La primera clara (y casi la única) fue para King con un balón a la cruceta en un disparo precioso. Solamente Gonzalo titular, Palacios y Manuel Ángel en el banquillo. No fue, sin embargo, hasta el minuto 80 cuando se decidió el partido. Y fue en una acción individual brillante de Oscar Bobb, ex del Manchester City. El noruego tiró de quiebros y recortes para eludir a su defensa y definir al palo largo, superando a Rushworth. Para el Fulham es su segundo triunfo consecutivo en Premier, ambos ante dos recién ascendidos: Hull City y Coventry. Y ambos, con el mismo resultado: 1-0 y 0-1. Suficiente para que Arbeloa coja algo de aire en Craven Cottage.
